  • Sealed container: Bar oil is sticky and a nightmare on the compartment floor — keep the cap tight.
  • Funnel/spout: Most jugs have a built-in pour spout.
  • The saw's oil reservoir cap: Don't confuse it with the fuel cap — they're usually clearly marked, but read the label.
🏷️Alternate names

"Bar oil," "bar & chain oil," "saw oil," "Stihl oil" (brand).

🔀
Rookie Mistake — Filling the Wrong ReservoirTwo-stroke fuel goes in the FUEL tank. Bar oil goes in the OIL tank. Putting bar oil in the fuel tank seizes the engine. Putting fuel in the oil tank starves the chain of lubrication and burns the bar. Read the caps. Both saws have the same arrangement — don't mix them up.
🌡️
Cold-Weather Bar OilBar oil thickens in winter. Some departments keep a thinner winter-grade in cold months. If the oiler isn't keeping up in a December cut, that's the reason.
Extra Chainsaw Chains
AKA: Spare chains, backup chains, "the black box"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Spare chains for the chainsaw, kept in a black box next to the saw itself. When you hit a nail, a piece of embedded rebar, or you just plain dull the chain mid-cut, you don't stop to sharpen — you swap the chain and keep working. Roof time is borrowed time; a dull chain that bogs down halfway through a vent cut gets somebody hurt.

🧩Parts
  • Black storage box: Keeps the spare chains coiled, oiled, and separated from everything else so they don't tangle or rust.
  • Chain(s): Matched to the bar length of the chainsaw on this rig — verify pitch and gauge before you buy or swap in a replacement from another rig.
🏷️Alternate names

"Spare chains," "backup chains," "the extra chain," "the black box" (referring to where they're stored).

🔗
Rookie Mistake — Grabbing Any Chain That Fits the BoxNot every chain that physically fits is rated for this bar or this saw. Wrong pitch or gauge will either not seat right or will run loose and derail off the bar mid-cut — on a roof, that's a chain flying at your face or your partner's. Check the chain matches the saw before you're up there needing it.
🔋

DS Compartment 3 (Over Wheel) — Bottom Shelf

Pics
Cordless Power Tool Set · Impacts · Grinder · Recip Saw · Blades · Bits · Charger
1/2" Impact Wrench
AKA: Half-inch impact, impact gun, impact driver (loosely), "the half-inch"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A high-torque cordless impact wrench with a 1/2" square drive anvil — designed to remove and install heavy fasteners. Lug nuts, large bolts, U-bolts, suspension hardware, agricultural and industrial fasteners. Use it for vehicle stabilization (removing wheels to drop a car flat onto cribbing), industrial extrications, and forcible entry on bolted assemblies.

🧩Parts
  • 1/2" anvil: The square output drive that holds the impact sockets.
  • Battery pack: Lithium-ion. Watch the fuel gauge.
  • Forward/reverse switch: Set it BEFORE you pull the trigger.
  • Variable speed trigger & mode switch: Higher-end units have torque settings.
  • Belt hook: Don't break your fingers fishing the gun out of a bag.
🏷️Alternate names

"Impact gun," "1/2" impact," "the gun," "rattle gun," "Milwaukee" or "DeWalt" (brand-as-generic).

🔩
Rookie Mistake — Using a Hand Socket on an ImpactStandard chrome sockets are NOT rated for impact use. They shatter under repeated hammering and send shrapnel into hands and faces. Only use impact-rated (matte black) sockets on this tool. Always. The cost of an impact socket is cheaper than an ER visit.
📍
Know Where the Bits LiveThe rated black titanium impact bits/sockets for this gun are stored in the rear officer's side compartment, not in this compartment. If you grab the gun and go, you'll show up without the right sockets. Grab both on the way.
🔄
Forward to Tighten, Reverse to LoosenStandard rule. Verify the direction switch every time before you pull the trigger — backing a fastener off when you meant to tighten it (and vice versa) will cost you time you don't have.
1/4" Impact Driver (with Bits)
AKA: Impact driver, quarter-inch impact, hex driver, "the little one"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A smaller, lighter cordless impact driver with a 1/4" hex-shank chuck for driving screws, lag bolts, and smaller fasteners. Used to drive deck screws into shoring/cribbing, build up wood box cribs, secure plywood, and any task where the 1/2" is overkill.

🧩Parts
  • 1/4" hex quick-change chuck: Sleeve pulls back to accept a hex-shank bit.
  • Bit case: Stays with the tool — Phillips, square, Torx, hex bits, magnetic holders. If a bit goes missing, replace it before the case goes back.
  • Battery, trigger, forward/reverse: Standard cordless layout.
🏷️Alternate names

"Impact driver," "quarter-inch impact," "screw gun" (informal), "hex driver."

🧰
Rookie Mistake — Losing Bits in the BagBits roll, bits drop, bits live forever in the bottom of jumpsuit pockets. A missing #2 Phillips at 0300 on a wind shoring job means somebody else is doing your work. Bits go back in the case at the end of every use. If the case has the slot, fill the slot.
🧲
Magnetic Bit Holder Beats Bare BitsThe magnetic holder keeps the screw on the bit while you start the driver one-handed. Essential when you're up on a ladder or in a confined space holding cribbing with one hand.
Angle Grinder
AKA: Grinder, side grinder, 4-1/2 grinder, disc grinder, "the grinder"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A handheld grinder running a small (typically 4-1/2") abrasive or cutting wheel. Used for precision metal cutting where the K12 is too big or too violent — cutting a stuck bolt on a steering column, slicing a small piece of rebar, grinding a burr off a sharp edge, cutting a lock shackle. More controlled than the K12 in tight spaces.

🧩Parts
  • Disc/wheel: Cutting (thin) or grinding (thick). Different jobs, different discs.
  • Wheel guard: Positioned to deflect sparks away from your body. Don't remove it. Ever.
  • Side handle: Two-hand operation, every time.
  • Spindle lock: Press to lock the spindle for wheel changes. NEVER while the tool is running.
  • Trigger/paddle switch: Some have a deadman paddle — release it, it stops.
  • Battery or cord: Know which.
🏷️Alternate names

"Grinder," "angle grinder," "4-1/2 grinder," "side grinder," "disc grinder."

💥
Rookie Mistake — Removing the Guard for Better AccessThe guard exists because angle grinder wheels shatter. Probie removes the guard "for clearance," wheel disintegrates at 11,000 RPM, shrapnel goes into the femoral. There is no scenario where the guard comes off. None. Pick a smaller wheel or a different tool.
👀
Full Face Shield, Not Just GlassesGrinders throw a stream of hot metal particles AND occasionally a chunk of disc. Safety glasses help. A full face shield over the glasses is what the experienced guys wear. Sparks in the eye through the corner of safety glasses still happen.
Reciprocating Saw (with Metal & Wood Blades)
AKA: Sawzall, recip, reciprocating saw, "the Sawzall"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A handheld reciprocating saw — push/pull blade action — that handles almost anything you point at it with the right blade. Cuts metal, wood, plastic, drywall, copper pipe, vehicle pillars, fence wire. Probably the most versatile cutting tool on this rig. Used heavily in extrications for things that don't justify pulling out the Hurst tools.

🧩Parts
  • Blade: Wood blades have fewer, larger teeth. Metal blades have many fine teeth. Match the blade to the material.
  • Blade clamp/quick-release: Some require a key; modern units twist open.
  • Shoe (front foot): Rests against the workpiece — pressing the shoe IN reduces blade chatter.
  • Variable speed trigger: Start slow on metal, ramp up.
  • Orbital/straight selector (some units): Orbital action is for wood; straight action is for metal.
  • Battery or cord.
🏷️Alternate names

"Sawzall" (Milwaukee brand-as-generic, used everywhere), "recip saw," "reciprocating saw," "tiger saw" (older term), "hognose."

⚙️
Rookie Mistake — Wrong Blade for the JobA wood blade on metal stalls the saw and dulls the blade in two seconds. A metal blade on wood is slow and walks off the cut line. Look at the blade box: blue/silver bi-metal blades for metal, dark-tooth coarse blades for wood. Pick on purpose.
🌡️
Hot Blade After a Long CutA recip blade after cutting steel for thirty seconds is hot enough to burn a hand badly. Let it cool or grab the body of the saw, not the blade. Skin sticks to hot steel.
🩻
Watch for Hidden HazardsRecip saws will happily cut through electrical wires, gas lines, hydraulic lines, brake lines, and people you didn't know were there. Before you plunge into a wall or a vehicle, know what's behind it.
Spare Blades (Recip / Circ / Etc.)
AKA: Blade kit, spare blades, "the blade box"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Spare cutting blades for the reciprocating saw, circular saw, and other powered cutters. Stored together so when you dull, bend, or break a blade mid-cut you can swap and keep moving. A used or broken blade is a bookmark — you replace it immediately, you don't put it back to "use later."

🧩Parts & categories
  • Wood-cutting recip blades: Few large teeth, aggressive.
  • Metal-cutting recip blades: Many fine teeth, bi-metal.
  • Demolition/multi-material blades: Will cut wood with embedded nails.
  • Carbide-grit blades: Tile, fiberglass, cement board.
  • Spare circular saw blades: Wood and possibly metal-cutting carbide.
🏷️Alternate names

"Blade box," "spares," "consumables." Blades have labels on the blade body — TPI (teeth per inch) and the recommended material printed on them.

🧹
Rookie Mistake — Putting a Dull or Broken Blade BackThe next person to grab a blade out of that case is doing it at 0300 in the rain. If it's dull, snapped, or bent, it goes in the trash. Mark it bad, dispose of it, restock from spare stock during rig check. Don't make somebody else discover your dull blade at the worst moment.
Battery Charger
AKA: Charger, charging station, battery dock, "the charger"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The on-board charging station for the cordless tool battery packs. Keeps batteries topped off so when you grab the impact, the grinder, or the recip, it works. The Squad runs almost everything off batteries — a dead pack stops the job cold.

🧩Parts
  • Charging cradle/dock: Battery slides in and locks.
  • Status LED: Red = charging, green = ready, blinking = fault.
  • Cooling fan (some chargers): Cools a hot pack before it'll start charging.
  • Power cord: Plugs into the inverter/shore power.
🏷️Alternate names

"Charger," "charging station," "battery dock." Brand chargers only fit their own brand's packs — verify compatibility on rig check.

🪫
Rookie Mistake — Pulling a Battery and Not Putting It Back to ChargeThis is the single most common Squad sin. You use a battery, you put it BACK on the charger so the next crew has a full pack. Probies who treat batteries like one-time consumables get the truck stuck halfway through an extrication. Battery in, battery on charger. Every time.
🔥
Damaged Lithium Batteries BurnIf a pack is cracked, swollen, leaking, or hot to the touch, take it OUT of service and notify the Lieutenant. Damaged lithium-ion batteries can spontaneously combust and burn the rig. Don't charge a damaged pack. Don't toss it in the trash.
Drill / Driver Bits
AKA: Bits, bit kit, drill index, "the bit case"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The assortment of driver bits and drill bits used with the smaller 1/4" impact driver — Phillips, square, Torx, hex, slotted, plus twist drill bits for steel and wood. Used for everything from building cribbing to opening a screwed-shut door to drilling weep holes in a vehicle. Don't confuse this case with the impact-rated sockets for the 1/2" gun — different tool, different bits.

🧩Parts & types
  • Phillips bits (#1, #2, #3): Most common driver bit, sized to the screw.
  • Square/Robertson bits: Common on construction screws.
  • Torx bits: Star pattern, common in automotive.
  • Hex bits: Allen-head fasteners.
  • Twist drill bits: Cutting holes in metal/wood.
  • Magnetic bit holder: Extends reach, holds the screw.
🏷️Alternate names

"Bits," "driver bits," "drill index" (the case), "tips" (small Phillips bits).

🔩
Rookie Mistake — Stripping the FastenerWrong-size Phillips on a screw cams out and strips the head in two seconds. Now you can't get the screw out at all. Match the size. If a #2 is sloppy, try a #3. If the head is starting to round, switch to vice grips or a screw extractor before it gets worse.
🫁

Driver's Side Rear Cabinet — Air Cascade

Pics
Cascade Controls · Adapters · Towel · Quick Connect · O-Rings · Air Hose · Power Cord
Cascade Controls
AKA: Cascade panel, fill panel, bottle fill station, "the cascade"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The cascade is a bank of high-pressure breathing-air storage cylinders mounted on the Squad, plumbed to a fill station with regulators and gauges. It's how we refill empty SCBA bottles on scene at a long-duration job. Without cascade, every empty SCBA is a trip back to the station. With cascade, the rig is a mobile fill plant.

🧩Parts
  • Storage bottles: Several large high-pressure cylinders of breathing air.
  • Inlet/supply regulator: Reduces high storage pressure to fill-line pressure.
  • Fill station / containment cabinet: A blast-rated enclosure where the SCBA cylinder is placed during filling. Door MUST be closed during fill.
  • Pressure gauges: One for supply (storage), one for the cylinder being filled.
  • Fill valve / control valve: Slowly admits air into the SCBA cylinder.
  • Bleed/vent valve: Bleeds pressure off the fill line so you can disconnect.
  • Whip hose / fill connector: The CGA fitting that mates to the SCBA bottle valve.
🏷️Alternate names

"Cascade," "fill station," "bottle fill," "high-pressure air station," "air bank."

💣
Rookie Mistake — Filling Outside the Containment BoxSCBA cylinders pressurized to 4500 psi can fail catastrophically. Containment cabinets are blast-rated to protect the operator if a bottle ruptures. Filling with the door open, or filling on the bench because the cabinet is "too slow," has killed people. CLOSED door. Every fill. No exceptions.
🌡️
Fill SLOWLYFast fills heat the air in the cylinder. Hot fills mean the cylinder shows full but cools to below service pressure. Worse, rapid filling stresses the cylinder. Open the fill valve slowly. Watch the gauge. Stop short of overfill — bottles cool and settle.
📅
Check Hydro Date on the BottleComposite SCBA cylinders have a service life and require periodic hydrostatic testing. Out-of-date bottles do NOT get filled. Read the stamp. If you can't find it, ask. An expired bottle is dangerous AND a regulatory violation.
Adapters — Air Reel, Scuba, & Boom Fill
AKA: Cascade adapters, fill adapters, fittings, "the adapter set"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Specialty fittings that adapt the cascade output to different fill needs. The air reel adapter connects to a long air hose reel for supplying low-pressure breathing air (think confined-space SAR work). The scuba adapter fits the threads on dive cylinders (different from SCBA — DON'T mix them up). The boom fill adapter connects to the boom truck / aerial fill system. Each adapter is a different thread pattern and rating.

🧩Parts
  • Each adapter body: Machined fitting with appropriate CGA or proprietary threads.
  • O-rings/seals: Pre-fill, check for cracks or missing rings.
  • Storage pouches/holders: Each adapter has a home — return it to that home.
🏷️Alternate names

"Cascade adapters," "fill adapters," "fittings," "CGA adapters." Different brands and applications use different CGA numbers — labels matter.

🧪
Rookie Mistake — Filling SCUBA Bottles With SCBA AirSCUBA-grade air is held to a different standard than SCBA breathing air (moisture and CO limits). Filling a dive bottle from an unrated source can kill the diver. Confirm your cascade is rated for the fill you're making. If you're unsure, ASK before you connect.
⚠️
Don't Force a Thread That Doesn't MatchIf the adapter doesn't thread on smoothly with two fingers, it's the wrong adapter or it's cross-threaded. Forcing it ruins the fitting and creates a leak path under high pressure. Stop, check, switch adapters.
Towel
AKA: Cascade towel, fill towel, "the rag"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A clean towel kept with the cascade. Used to wipe moisture and grit off SCBA cylinder valves and fittings before connecting them to the fill station. Dirt and water in a high-pressure connection are bad news. Looks like nothing — actually matters.

🧩Parts
  • Just a clean towel. Keep it clean. If it gets contaminated with oil, fuel, or hydraulic fluid, replace it.
🏷️Alternate names

"Fill towel," "cascade rag," "the rag."

🛢️
Rookie Mistake — Using a Greasy Shop RagAny hydrocarbon — oil, grease, gasoline, even hand lotion residue — on a high-pressure oxygen or air fitting can spontaneously combust under pressure. This is called "adiabatic ignition" and it has burned hands clean off and ruptured cylinders. The cascade towel is for cascade work, period. If somebody used it to wipe up bar oil, throw it out.
Quick Connect for SCBA
AKA: Quick fill, SCBA fill adapter, cascade fill connector, "fill line"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A high-pressure quick-connect/disconnect fitting that interfaces the cascade system directly with SCBA cylinders for on-scene refills. Instead of swapping bottles, this lets you fill a cylinder right at the rig during extended operations — structural fires, prolonged extrication, anything that burns through air. The fitting seats and seals under pressure.

🧩Parts
  • Quick-disconnect body: The mating half that seats into the SCBA cylinder fill nipple.
  • Valve/shutoff: Controls flow — open after connection, close before disconnecting.
  • High-pressure hose: Connects the fitting to the cascade panel output.
  • Dust cap: Keeps the fitting clean and contamination-free when stored — cap it every time.
🏷️Alternate names

"Quick fill," "cascade fill adapter," "SCBA fill connector," "fill line." You'll also hear "hook up the quick connect" as shorthand for the whole fill procedure.

☠️
Rookie Mistake — Disconnecting Under PressureNEVER yank a quick-connect fitting while there is still pressure in the fill line. Close the cascade valve first, let the line vent, then disconnect. A high-pressure fitting that separates under load can cause severe injury. Establish the sequence and never skip it: close valve → vent → disconnect. Every time.
🧹
Keep It Clean and CappedContamination introduced into the breathing air system is a life safety issue. Cap the fitting after every use. Inspect the o-ring on the fitting before each fill — a damaged o-ring means a leaking connection at 4500 PSI.
O-Rings
AKA: Seals, gaskets (informal), o-ring kit, cascade seals
+
📖What it is & what it does

Rubber torus seals that maintain airtight connections throughout the cascade system and SCBA fill fittings. At operating pressures of 4500 PSI, a compromised o-ring doesn't just leak — it fails. These are your first line of defense against air system failures during extended operations. Keep them stocked, inspect them routinely, replace them without hesitation.

🧩Parts
  • O-ring body: The rubber torus — inspect for cuts, nicks, flattening, or brittleness.
  • Various sizes: Different connections require specific o-ring sizes — don't substitute.
  • O-ring pick/removal tool: For removing a seated o-ring without damaging the groove.
🏷️Alternate names

"O-ring," "seal," sometimes called "gasket" informally (gaskets are flat — o-rings are round, but don't waste time correcting people on scene). In cascade context you'll hear "check your o-rings" or "swap the o-ring."

☠️
Rookie Mistake — Reusing a Damaged O-RingIf you find a nicked, flattened, or cracked o-ring, replace it. Do not reinstall it. At 4500 PSI, a bad o-ring doesn't leak slowly — it can fail suddenly, blow the fitting, and vent compressed air violently. Keep spares stocked. Check them every time you check the cascade.
🛢️
Use the Right LubricantIf an o-ring needs lubrication, use only silicone grease or lubricant rated for high-pressure air or oxygen service. Petroleum-based lubes degrade the rubber — and in oxygen-enriched systems, create a combustion hazard. Use what's approved. If you're not sure, ask before you guess.
Air Hose for SCBA Filling
AKA: Fill hose, cascade hose, "the fill line"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The dedicated high-pressure hose that runs from the cascade fill panel out to the quick-connect fitting used for filling SCBA cylinders on scene. This is the line under pressure every time a fill is happening — treat it with the same respect you give any charged air line.

🧩Parts
  • High-pressure hose body: Rated for cascade fill pressures.
  • Fittings at each end: One threads to the cascade panel, one mates to the quick-connect.
  • Protective sleeve/cover (if equipped): Guards against abrasion and kinking.
🏷️Alternate names

"Fill hose," "cascade hose," "fill line," "SCBA fill hose."

☠️
Rookie Mistake — Kinking or Standing on the HoseA kinked high-pressure hose restricts flow and stresses the hose wall. A hose someone's standing on, or that's laid across a sharp compartment edge, can chafe and fail under pressure. Route it clean — keep it off the ground where boots and tools can catch it.
🔍
Inspect Before Every FillLook the hose over for cuts, bulges, or soft spots before you charge it. A compromised high-pressure hose is a whip hazard if it fails under load.
Power Cord (from Generator)
AKA: Generator cord, shore cord, extension cord, "the gen cord"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A heavy-duty power cord that runs from the rig's onboard generator/inverter to equipment stored in the Air Cascade cabinet that needs electrical power — lighting, chargers, or accessory equipment tied to the cascade setup. Without it, anything electrical in this cabinet is dead weight.

🧩Parts
  • Cord body: Heavy-gauge, weather-rated jacket.
  • Male/female ends: Grounded plug connectors — inspect prongs and grounding pin before use.
  • Storage reel or coil strap: Keeps the cord from tangling in the compartment.
🏷️Alternate names

"Generator cord," "shore cord," "extension cord," "power lead."

⚡
Rookie Mistake — Running a Damaged CordA cracked jacket or a bent/missing ground pin turns a convenience item into a shock hazard, especially near the cascade's wet-towel-and-metal environment. Inspect before every use. Damaged cord goes out of service, not back in the cabinet.
🪜

Officer Front Compartments

Pics
Little Giant · Tarps · Step Cribbing · Cribbing Platforms · Oil Dry · Garbage Container
Little Giant Ladder
AKA: Multi-position ladder, articulating ladder, A-frame/extension combo, "the Little Giant"
+
📖What it is & what it does

An articulating multi-position ladder that converts between A-frame (stepladder), extension, scaffold, and 90° wall ladder configurations using hinged locking joints. Used for indoor work, attic access, basement entry, scaffold setup, and any task where a rigid extension ladder won't fit. Versatile, but heavy and fussier than a regular ladder.

🧩Parts
  • Outer and inner sections: The telescoping rails.
  • Hinge/lock at center: The articulating joint — set to A-frame, 90°, or extension position.
  • Hinge locks (red levers/buttons): POSITIVE engagement before climbing. Listen for the click.
  • Extension locks (rung locks): Spring-loaded, snap into rung holes.
  • Feet/levelers: Some models have adjustable feet for uneven ground.
  • Rails & rungs: Standard ladder anatomy.
🏷️Alternate names

"Little Giant" (brand-as-generic, the most common), "multi-position ladder," "articulating ladder," "combo ladder."

🩼
Rookie Mistake — Climbing With Hinge Locks Not Fully EngagedThe center hinge has positive locks. If you climb without verifying both sides are LOCKED, the ladder folds in the middle and dumps you. People break bones every year doing exactly this. Set the angle, listen for BOTH clicks, push down on the hinge to confirm. THEN climb.
⚖️
It Looks Stable Until It Isn'tThe A-frame configuration is forgiving. The 90° wall configuration is NOT — narrow base, easy to tip if you reach sideways. Belt-buckle stays between the rails. Move the ladder, don't lean.
Tarps
AKA: Salvage covers, salvage tarps, ground covers, "the tarps"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Heavy waterproof covers used to protect a victim's property from water damage during fire suppression and overhaul. We throw tarps over furniture, electronics, and family heirlooms before water hits them. They're also used as ground covers for tool layouts, patient packaging, and laying out gear during long extrications. Salvage work is part of the job — saving the homeowner's wedding photos from the hose stream is real customer service.

🧩Parts
  • Tarp body: Vinyl or coated canvas, water-resistant.
  • Grommets: Reinforced eyelets at corners for tie-downs.
  • Hemmed edges: Reinforced corners and edges resist tearing.
  • Folded/rolled storage: Stored neat so they deploy fast.
🏷️Alternate names

"Salvage covers," "salvage tarps," "covers," "ground cover."

💧
Rookie Mistake — Not Folding Tarps Back ProperlyTarps that go back in the compartment soaked, balled up, and dirty mildew and rot. Then they don't lay flat when you need them. After use, hose them off, shake them dry, fold or roll them back into shape, and report wet tarps to the Lieutenant. A moldy tarp is useless.
🎯
Deploy Early, Not LateBest time to throw a salvage cover is BEFORE the engine company opens the line. Train yourself to anticipate water — the second you see flame, your eyes should be looking for what to cover.
Step Cribbing / Chocks
AKA: Step chocks, cribs, blocks, wood cribbing, wedges, "the cribbing"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Wood (sometimes plastic/composite) blocks of varied sizes used to stabilize vehicles and structures. Squares, rectangles, step chocks, and wedges that you stack and shim under a vehicle, against a load, or beneath a cut to create a solid, predictable resting surface. The single most important principle of vehicle extrication is "lift an inch, crib an inch" — every change in elevation gets cribbed BEFORE you trust it.

🧩Parts & types
  • Standard cribs (4x4, 2x4): Stacked in log-cabin "box cribbing" pattern for vertical lifts.
  • Step chocks: Stair-step shaped blocks for under rocker panels.
  • Wedges: Tapered, driven in to take up the last bit of slack — never load-bearing alone.
  • Color coding (some departments): Different colors for different lengths/sizes.
🏷️Alternate names

"Cribs," "blocks," "step chocks" (specifically the stair-shaped ones), "wedges" (the tapered ones), "shim wedges."

🚗
Rookie Mistake — "Lift, Then Crib" Done WrongPeople get crushed when a jack slips. Probies hold the load on the jack while they crib — wrong. You lift ONE inch, slide a crib UNDER, lower the load ONTO the crib, repeat. The crib is the load-bearer, not the jack. The jack is only a temporary lifter. Mantra: "lift an inch, crib an inch."
📦
Cribbing Pattern MattersStack box-crib style — each layer 90° to the layer below, like Lincoln Logs. Stacks that lean are stacks that fail. Keep the load over the center of the stack. Cribbing higher than three times its base width is unstable — switch to taller pieces or build wider.
🧱
Cracked or Oil-Soaked Cribbing Goes Out of ServiceWood absorbs fuel and oil at MVA scenes. Hydrocarbon-soaked cribbing is a fire hazard and structurally compromised. Inspect after every use. If it's cracked, split, soaked, or worse-for-wear, it goes in the burn pile — not back on the rig.
Cribbing Platforms
AKA: Cribbing base plates, platform blocks, crib bases, "the platforms"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Large flat base platforms used as the foundation layer for cribbing stacks. They spread the load over a larger surface area and prevent the bottom of the crib stack from punching into soft ground, asphalt, or any surface that might give way under concentrated point loads. Think of them as the footer for a cribbing column — without a solid base, your whole stack can sink, tilt, or fail.

🧩Parts
  • Platform body: Wide flat block or panel — wood, composite, or HDPE plastic depending on department.
  • Surface texture: Rough or grooved to grip the cribbing stack above it and the ground below.
  • Handles / cutouts (some models): For easy one-hand carry.
  • Rating: Rated to a specific load capacity per the manufacturer.
🏷️Alternate names

"Cribbing base," "platform block," "base plate," "crib foundation," "crib platform."

🏗️
Rookie Mistake — Building Cribbing on Soft Ground Without a PlatformA 4x4 crib stack on soft soil or asphalt will punch straight into the surface the moment load is applied. The platform distributes that load so the stack doesn't sink. If you skip the platform on a hot asphalt roadway in July, your crib stack goes INTO the asphalt. Platform first — always.
📐
Center the Stack on the PlatformA crib stack built off-center on a platform is an unstable crib stack. Keep the base of your cribbing column centered on the platform. Eccentric loading tilts the stack and transfers force to the platform edge, which can flip it.
Oil Dry (Absorbent)
AKA: Speedy Dry, absorbent, floor-dry, kitty litter, "the absorbent"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A granular absorbent — typically clay-based, like cat litter — used to soak up spilled fluids at MVA scenes (oil, antifreeze, fuel residue) and restore traction on slick surfaces. Spread it over the spill, give it a few minutes, then sweep/shovel it into the spill kit container for disposal.

🧩Parts
  • Bagged or bucketed absorbent: Granules ranging from coarse to fine.
  • Closure/scoop: Most containers have a built-in pour spout or scoop.
🏷️Alternate names

"Speedy Dry" (brand-as-generic, most common name on jobs), "Oil-Dri," "absorbent," "floor-dry," "kitty litter" (informal — clay litter does work in a pinch).

🚯
Rookie Mistake — Sweeping Saturated Absorbent Into a Storm DrainThe whole point of absorbent is to KEEP the contamination out of the waterway. Saturated absorbent that gets swept into a storm drain pollutes the very thing you were trying to protect, and your department now owns an EPA violation. Sweep it into a bag or the spill kit container for proper disposal.
⏱️
Give It Time to WorkThrowing absorbent down and immediately sweeping is pointless. Spread it, wait three to five minutes for it to actually absorb, THEN sweep. Heavy spills may need a second application.
Garbage Container
AKA: Trash can, refuse container, debris bin, "the can"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A dedicated container on the rig for collecting scene debris — broken glass, plastic shards from extrications, soiled gloves and gauze, the saturated absorbent from oil-dry cleanup. Keeps trash off the roadway and out of the bystanders' yards. Part of leaving a scene cleaner than we found it.

🧩Parts
  • Container body: Plastic or metal can with a lid.
  • Lid: Keeps debris from blowing out.
  • Liner bag (when used): Makes disposal cleaner.
🏷️Alternate names

"Trash can," "garbage can," "debris bin," "the can."

🩹
Rookie Mistake — Mixing Sharps and Biohazards With Regular DebrisBloody gauze, used IV catheters, broken bottles, and contaminated PPE do NOT go in the same container with ordinary trash. They need biohazard or sharps disposal. Mixing them creates an exposure risk for whoever empties the can later. Know the difference. When in doubt, ask the medic.
🛠️

Transverse — Officer Side Shelf

Pics
Hurst Ram Tool · Hurst Cutter · Hurst Spreader · B-Post Tool (V-Rocker) · Windows Punch
Hurst Ram Tool
AKA: Ram, hydraulic ram, telescoping ram, Hurst ram, "the ram"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A hydraulic linear ram from the Hurst (Jaws of Life) family used to push and lift heavy loads — pushing a dashboard off a trapped patient's legs, spreading two structural members apart, lifting a heavy column. The ram extends in a straight line under tremendous pressure when the operator squeezes the trigger.

🧩Parts
  • Cylinder body: Houses the hydraulic piston.
  • Telescoping shaft(s): Extend out as you trigger the tool.
  • Push tip / extension tips: Threaded on the business end. Some are pointed, some are flat.
  • Base / butt: Wide foot for purchase against a structure.
  • Hydraulic coupler: Connects to the pump hose. Quick-connects must be FULLY seated.
  • Trigger/dead-man valve: Release the trigger, ram stops.
  • Pressure relief: Built-in, protects against over-pressure.
🏷️Alternate names

"Ram," "hydraulic ram," "telescoping ram," "Hurst ram," "Jaws ram." Hurst is one major brand — Holmatro and others make equivalents.

💥
Rookie Mistake — Ram Walking Off the AnchorIf your push surface isn't seated SOLID, the ram can kick out under load and rocket out at lethal speed. Find a structural anchor — frame rail, B-pillar at the base — not a piece of body panel. Set the ram, take pressure, verify it's not migrating before you commit.
🦵
Mind the PatientRams move things that were previously stable. That dashboard you just pushed up was holding the patient's leg in a certain position; when you move it, the leg moves. Coordinate with the medic. Communicate before you trigger.
Hurst Cutter
AKA: Cutters, Jaws cutter, Hurst cutter, hydraulic cutters, "the cutters"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The hydraulic cutter from the Hurst family — a heavy-duty alligator-style cutter that severs structural metal: vehicle posts, roof rails, steering columns, seat frames. The cutting force at the tips of those jaws is measured in tons. Used in extrication to peel a vehicle apart so we can access a trapped patient.

🧩Parts
  • Cutting jaws / blades: Hardened forged steel. NEVER cut through the very tip — bites toward the throat are stronger.
  • Pivot pin: The structural hinge.
  • Hydraulic cylinder body: Houses the actuator.
  • Hose couplers: Lock onto the pump hoses.
  • Trigger/handle: Dead-man operation.
  • Carrying handle & balance point.
🏷️Alternate names

"Cutters," "Jaws of Life" (popular slang, technically refers to the original product line), "Hurst cutter." Holmatro/Amkus/Genesis make competitive equivalents.

⚡
Rookie Mistake — Cutting Through High-Strength Steel Without KnowingModern vehicle B-pillars contain ultra-high-strength steel and boron alloys that older cutters CANNOT cut. The cutter will stall, the jaws can chip, and you waste critical minutes. Know your tool's rating. If it's not cutting on first squeeze, STOP and re-evaluate position or switch tools.
🔥
Hybrid & EV Vehicles — Color-Coded CablesOrange = high voltage. NEVER cut an orange cable. NEVER cut into the battery box. Reference the manufacturer's emergency response guide. Cutting high-voltage cable will kill you and start a thermal-runaway battery fire that water won't extinguish.
🛡️
PPE Every Time — Visor DownSteel under cutter pressure can fail explosively. Visor down. Crew shielded with a tarp or shield. Patient covered. Cutter operators get hit with shrapnel — protect everyone.
Hurst Spreader
AKA: Spreaders, Jaws of Life, Hurst spreader, "the spreaders"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The hydraulic spreader — the iconic "Jaws of Life" tool. Hooked tips that open from a closed position with thousands of pounds of force. Used to peel doors off vehicles, pop locks, pry sheet metal apart, spread two pinching surfaces. The spreader bites in, then forces open.

🧩Parts
  • Spreader tips / arms: Curved, hooked, hardened.
  • Inner tip surfaces: Where most of the force is. Bites work best with the tips fully inserted.
  • Body / hydraulic cylinder.
  • Pivot pin and linkage.
  • Hose couplers, trigger, handle.
  • Threaded tip mounts (some models): Different tips for different jobs.
🏷️Alternate names

"Spreaders," "Jaws," "Jaws of Life," "Hurst spreaders."

⛓️
Rookie Mistake — Tips Slipping OffSlick wet metal, painted surfaces, and shallow purchase points cause tips to slip explosively. The tool fires out of the gap and hits whoever's standing in the way. Set the tips DEEP. Crew clear of the firing line. Hand on the handle, never under the tip.
🔌
Hose Couplers — Locked & BledIf the couplers aren't fully seated or there's pressure trapped in the line, the tool won't operate or the hoses won't connect. Verify the pump is at the correct setting and the couplers click home. If the spreader won't open, STOP — don't force it.
B-Post Tool
AKA: V-Rocker, B-pillar tool, post tool, side-impact tool, "the B-post"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Also called the V-Rocker on this rig — a specialty tool used to displace or attach to the B-pillar (the post between the front and rear doors of a 4-door vehicle) during extrication. On Squad 61 it's set up specifically as a stabilization platform for the Ram Tool, giving the ram a solid base to push against instead of unsupported sheet metal. Helps spread or remove the B-post when it's pinning a patient or blocking patient access.

🧩Parts
  • Capture jaws or hooks: Engage the B-pillar.
  • Mounting/coupling point: Connects to the Hurst spreader or ram.
  • Locking pin / set screw: Holds the tool to the spreader.
🏷️Alternate names

"V-Rocker" (this rig's name for it), "B-pillar tool," "post tool," "B-post displacer," "side-impact tool." Various brands.

🪛
Rookie Mistake — Not Knowing Which Tool Pairs With WhichOn this rig, the V-Rocker pairs with the Ram Tool as its stabilization base — not the spreader. If you grab it expecting to mate it to the spreader, you've just delayed the rescue figuring out why it doesn't fit. Pre-shift familiarization. Dry-fit it to the ram once a month so you know exactly how it goes together.
Windows Punch
AKA: Center punch, spring punch, glass punch, "the punch"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A spring-loaded punch that fires a hardened steel tip with enough force to shatter tempered (side & rear) automotive glass. Press the tip against a corner of the side window and the spring releases — the window crumbles into pebbles. Use it on the corner of the car window, not the middle of the pane. The fastest way to make access into a vehicle when the doors won't open and you need in NOW. Will NOT work on the laminated windshield (or laminated side glass on newer vehicles).

🧩Parts
  • Body / barrel: Contains the spring.
  • Striker tip: Hardened point that breaks the glass.
  • Adjustment cap (some models): Sets the spring tension.
  • Pocket clip: So it goes on your gear.
🏷️Alternate names

"Center punch," "window punch," "spring punch," "glass punch," "ResQMe" (small keychain version), "auto-resetting center punch."

🔍
Rookie Mistake — Punching the WindshieldWindshields are LAMINATED safety glass. The punch will only chip it, not break it through. Side windows and rear windows are TEMPERED — those shatter. Use the punch on the side, not the front. To breach the windshield you need a glass saw or to remove it whole.
👁️
Cover the Patient FirstTempered glass crumbles into small pebbles but they still go in eyes and open wounds. Cover the patient's face with a salvage cover or tarp before you fire the punch. Verify the patient knows what's about to happen — that LOUD pop right next to their head is alarming.
📐
Aim For the Lower CornerThe lower corner of the side window is the weakest part and most predictable break point — that's the corner the doc calls out too. Don't waste a strike on the middle of the pane.
🔧

Transverse — Long Shelf

Pics
Tow Hooks & Chain · Akron Lights · Jacks · Air Chisel · RIT Pack · Submersible · Road Salt · Bolt Cutters · Life Safety Rope
2× Buckets — Tow Hooks & Chain
AKA: Tow chain buckets, chain buckets, tow hook kit
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two buckets, each holding a tow hook and length of chain, for hooking onto a vehicle frame or axle to drag, right, or reposition it during an extrication or MVA scene.

🧩Parts
  • Tow hook: Heavy forged hook, rated for the load — attaches to a frame point or tow eye.
  • Chain: Grade-rated chain, coiled in the bucket to stay untangled and ready to pay out.
  • Bucket: Keeps the chain contained and the hook from banging around the compartment.
🏷️Alternate names

"Chain buckets," "tow hooks," "the tow kit."

⛓️
Rookie Mistake — Hooking to the Wrong PointA tow hook on anything but a rated frame point or tow eye can tear loose under load and turn into a projectile. Know your attachment points before you pull. And never stand in the bight of a chain under tension — if it lets go, it whips.
2× Akron Lights
AKA: Akron scene lights, portable scene lights, telescoping lights, work lights, "Akrons"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Portable telescoping scene lights — Akron is the brand. Set them up around an extrication or working scene to flood the work area with light independent of the roof-mounted tower. They run off generator/inverter power and can be aimed anywhere they're needed.

🧩Parts
  • Lamp head: LED or halogen.
  • Telescoping pole: Adjustable height with twist or clamp lock.
  • Base/tripod: Folding legs for stability.
  • Power cord: Long lead with grounded plug.
  • Switch: On the head or in-line on the cord.
🏷️Alternate names

"Akrons," "Akron lights," "portable scene lights," "work lights," "tripod lights."

⚡
Rookie Mistake — Trip Hazards From CordsA dozen cords running every direction across an extrication scene is a broken ankle waiting to happen. Run cords against walls, tape them down across walking paths, or route them OVER the work area. The medic dropping a patient because they tripped on YOUR light cord is on you.
🛢️
Halogen Heads BurnOlder halogen Akrons run hot enough to burn skin. LED replacements are cooler. Know which you have. If you can pick up the head bare-handed after thirty seconds running, it's LED. Otherwise: don't grab the head.
2× High Lift Jacks / Farmer Jacks
AKA: Hi-Lift, farm jack, farmer jack, bumper jack, "the Hi-Lift"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two tall mechanical jacks with a long vertical beam and a ratcheting lift carriage — the classic "farm jack" or "farmer jack." Lifts heavy loads a long way (much higher than a bottle or scissor jack). Used for off-road extrications, raising vehicles in mud or uneven terrain, and any heavy lift where you need significant clearance. Carrying two lets you lift from both ends of a load at once.

🧩Parts
  • I-beam (post): The vertical column with the ratchet holes.
  • Carriage / runner: Climbs the beam with the lift nose.
  • Climbing pin / lift pin: Engages the beam holes.
  • Reversing latch (UP/DOWN): Switch position depending on whether you're lifting or lowering.
  • Handle / lever: The long bar you pump.
  • Base plate: The foot — bigger base on soft ground.
  • Lift nose / hook: Where the load sits.
🏷️Alternate names

"Hi-Lift" (brand-as-generic), "farm jack," "high-lift," "bumper jack," "kangaroo jack."

🦴
Rookie Mistake — Hi-Lift Handle Kicking BackThe Hi-Lift is famously the most dangerous jack on the market. If the load shifts or the lift nose slips, the handle WHIPS up violently and breaks jaws, teeth, eye sockets. Keep the handle vertical when not actively pumping. Stand to the SIDE of it, never in front. Both hands on the handle through the full stroke — never let it free-swing.
🪨
Crib As You LiftSame rule as any jack. The Hi-Lift is a temporary lifter, not a permanent support. Crib under the load the moment you have clearance. Never crawl under a Hi-Lift supported load.
4× Traffic Cones
AKA: Cones, traffic cones, pylons, witches' hats, "the cones"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Standard fluorescent orange (often with reflective collars) traffic cones used to set up an upstream taper at roadway incidents. Cones channel traffic away from the working scene, give us a buffer zone, and visibly mark the work area to oncoming drivers — particularly at night. Cones save lives. Specifically, they save firefighter lives.

🧩Parts
  • Cone body: PVC or rubber, weighted base.
  • Reflective collars: Retroreflective stripes for night visibility.
  • Base/weight: Keeps cone upright in wind/passing-vehicle airblast.
🏷️Alternate names

"Cones," "traffic cones," "pylons," "witches' hats" (UK/AUS slang).

🚗
Rookie Mistake — Setting the Cones Too CloseCones placed 10 feet upstream of the scene give an inattentive driver no time to react. At highway speeds the upstream taper needs to start hundreds of feet back. Follow your department's roadway incident SOP. Distance saves crews. Probies hit by cars are a recurring tragedy in this job.
🌬️
Wind & DraftsBig trucks blow cones over. Check your line, reset blown cones, and if cones won't stand up, switch to weighted bases or flares.
4× Res-Q-Jacks
AKA: Res-Q-Jack, struts, rescue struts, stabilization struts, "the struts"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Telescoping mechanical stabilization struts used to capture and lock a vehicle that's on its side, on its roof, or otherwise unstable. Set one or two at each end of the load to create a tripod-effect — the vehicle can't tip back onto the patient or the crew. Saves lives. Vehicles on their sides are unstable until stabilized; this is the tool that does it.

🧩Parts
  • Strut body (telescoping tubes): Inner and outer tubes that lock.
  • Pin lock: Quick-release pin engages predrilled holes.
  • Threaded fine adjustment: Lets you take up the last bit of slack to load the strut.
  • Base plate: Spiked or flat foot.
  • Head / attachment point: Hooks, claws, chains, ratchet straps connect to the vehicle.
  • Chain / strap: Anchors the head to the vehicle so the strut can't pop out.
🏷️Alternate names

"Rescue struts," "struts," "Res-Q-Jacks" (brand), "Paratech struts," "stab jacks."

🚙
Rookie Mistake — Working Inside a Vehicle Before It's StabilizedAn overturned car balanced on a bumper or door edge is a guillotine waiting to fall. People have been crushed climbing in to "just check on the patient." Stabilize FIRST, then work. Two struts minimum on a side-resting vehicle, four on a roof-resting vehicle. Anchor heads with chain to the chassis, not the body panels.
⛓️
Load the Strut Lightly — Don't Lift ItThe strut's job is to PREVENT movement, not LIFT the vehicle. Snug it. Take up slack. Don't crank it so hard the vehicle starts to rotate. Tension only — you're capturing the load where it is, not moving it.
2× Scissor Jacks
AKA: Scissor jack, screw jack, lift jack, "the scissors"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A mechanical scissor-style lifting jack — the same kind of jack that comes stowed in a passenger car for changing a tire. Slow but compact. Used for low-clearance lifts, raising a vehicle to drop it onto cribbing, or any task where a hydraulic jack is overkill.

🧩Parts
  • X-frame linkages: The four arms that scissor open as the screw closes.
  • Threaded screw: Operator turns to lift.
  • Crank or handle: Folds into the jack body.
  • Saddle (top): The lifting surface.
  • Base plate (bottom): The foot.
🏷️Alternate names

"Scissor jack," "screw jack," "trunk jack" (because it's what's in a car trunk).

🚙
Rookie Mistake — Trusting a Scissor Jack Long-TermThe scissor jack is for lifting, not for supporting. Their narrow base and high center of gravity makes them tippy under any side load. Lift, crib, lower onto crib. Don't leave a load on a scissor jack while you go work on something else.
Air Chisel
AKA: Air hammer, pneumatic chisel, panel cutter, "the chisel"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A pneumatic-powered hammer that drives a chisel bit at very high cycle rate. Runs off compressed air (cascade or a portable compressor). Used for cutting through vehicle sheet metal where saws or cutters won't fit — door skins, posts, body panels. Faster and more precise than chopping with an axe.

🧩Parts
  • Chisel bit / chisel: The cutting end. Various profiles: flat, panel cutter, bell-shaped.
  • Retainer / collar: Holds the bit in the chuck.
  • Trigger / valve: Variable cycle rate.
  • Air inlet fitting: Quick-connect to the air hose.
  • Regulator/coupler at supply: Sets working pressure.
  • Hearing protection requirement: Yes, every time.
🏷️Alternate names

"Air hammer," "pneumatic chisel," "panel cutter," "needle scaler" (different attachment, similar tool).

👂
Rookie Mistake — No Hearing ProtectionThe air chisel is loud enough to cause permanent hearing damage in a single extrication. Ear plugs or muffs. Every time. Your hearing won't grow back.
✋
Don't Trigger Off the WorkpieceThe chisel only cuts when the bit is loaded against the material. Triggering it in mid-air sends the bit flying or fractures the retainer. Bit on the work, THEN squeeze.
🪵
Never Dry-Fire It — Test on the Wood BlockThere's a wood block kept near the chisel specifically for function-testing the tool. Use it. Dry-firing the chisel — triggering it with no material loaded against the bit — slams the internals with nothing to absorb the impact and beats the tool to death. If you want to check that it's working, test it on the block, not in the air.
2× Buckets of Chain
AKA: Rescue chains, rigging chain, drag chain, "the chain"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Heavy-duty rated rigging chain stored in buckets so it deploys quickly without tangles. Used for pulling, dragging, anchoring, and connecting struts/winches to vehicles or structures. Chain doesn't stretch under load like rope, doesn't snap-back like cable, and won't burn through against a hot surface. Hooks at both ends.

🧩Parts
  • Chain links: Forged, rated alloy chain. Watch for cracked or stretched links.
  • Grab hooks: Slotted hooks that grab a chosen link for length adjustment.
  • Slip hooks / clevis hooks: Wider hooks for attaching to anchor points.
  • Rating tag: Each chain carries a stamped working load limit. KNOW IT.
  • Storage bucket: Chain feeds out, top of pile first. Coil it back loose.
🏷️Alternate names

"Rescue chain," "rigging chain," "drag chain," "grade-80" or "grade-100" chain (alloy ratings).

💢
Rookie Mistake — Shortening Chain With KnotsYou DO NOT tie knots in chain. A knot reduces working strength by half or more and causes failure. To shorten, fold the chain back through a grab hook. NEVER use a chain with stretched links, cracked welds, or a missing tag.
🪜
Standoff the AnchorChain wrapping a sharp corner WILL break on the corner. Pad the bend with cribbing or a sling protector to keep the chain off the sharp edge of the chassis.
RIT Airpack
AKA: RIT pack, RIT bag, FAST pack, rescue bottle, downed firefighter pack, "the RIT"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The Rapid Intervention Team air pack — a dedicated, ready-to-deploy SCBA assembly carried specifically for rescuing a downed firefighter. When a Mayday comes over the radio, this is what we grab. It's built around a 60-minute bottle at roughly 4,500 psi with a 25-foot transfill hose, so a rescuer can reach a downed firefighter without having to stand right on top of them. It typically includes a full air cylinder, that transfill hose to refill or supply a trapped firefighter's mask, a spare mask, and the harness needed to drag a victim out.

🧩Parts
  • SCBA cylinder (full): Verified full at every rig check.
  • Regulator / first stage: Plumbed to the supply.
  • Transfill hose (UAC — Universal Air Coupling): Connects to a downed firefighter's SCBA to refill or supply air.
  • Spare facepiece: If the downed firefighter's mask is damaged.
  • Carry handle / shoulder strap: For fast deployment by hand.
  • Drag harness or attachment loops: So the rescuer can move the victim.
  • Bag: Distinctive color (often red or orange) so it's not confused with a regular SCBA.
🏷️Alternate names

"RIT pack," "RIT bag," "FAST pack" (FAST = Firefighter Assist & Search Team), "rescue bottle," "downed firefighter pack," "Mayday pack."

🆘
Rookie Mistake — Treating the RIT Pack Like Spare GearThe RIT pack is NOT a backup SCBA. It is NOT for refilling your own bottle. It is locked, loaded, and untouched UNTIL a firefighter goes down. If you grab the RIT pack for routine use, you've just stripped the standby crew of their rescue gear. The day a Mayday comes in and the RIT bottle is half-empty because somebody borrowed it — that's the day somebody dies.
📋
Check It Every ShiftCylinder pressure, regulator function, mask seal, UAC fitting condition, bag closure. RIT pack rig check is not optional. You will not have time to discover a defect during a Mayday.
Dayton Submersible Pump
AKA: Sump pump, submersible, "the Dayton," "the sub pump"
+
📖What it is & what it does

An electric submersible pump — Dayton is the brand. Drops INTO standing water and pumps it out through a discharge hose. Used for basement floods, deep water removal where a wet vac is too slow, and any task where you need to move a high volume of water out and away. Pumps water faster than a wet vac because it's a continuous-duty unit.

🧩Parts
  • Pump body: Sealed motor inside, rests on the floor of the standing water.
  • Inlet screen / strainer: Keeps debris out of the impeller.
  • Discharge port: Threaded for the hose.
  • Discharge hose: Lay-flat or rigid hose to route water OUT.
  • Float switch (some models): Auto-shuts off when water level drops.
  • Power cord: Grounded plug — never operate without ground.
  • Carrying handle.
🏷️Alternate names

"Submersible pump," "sub pump," "sump pump," "Dayton" (brand).

⚡
Rookie Mistake — Running an Ungrounded PumpElectricity and water are not friends. Submersible pumps MUST be grounded, plugged into a GFCI-protected outlet, and inspected for cord damage before use. A pump with a frayed cord in a flooded basement is a death trap for the next person to step in the water. If the cord looks rough, the pump is out of service.
💨
Don't Run It DryThe pump cools using the water it's submerged in. Running it dry burns the motor in minutes. Float switches help; if there's no float, somebody watches the water level. When it gets low, you shut it down.
🛣️
Discharge Where It Goes AWAYDon't pump the water out of the basement and into the front yard six feet from the house. It'll run right back in. Route the discharge to a storm drain, downslope, or far enough to drain away.
Road Salt
AKA: Salt, ice melt, traction salt, "the salt"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Bagged road salt (typically sodium chloride or a calcium-chloride blend) for winter operations. Spread on icy patches around the rig and at scenes to give crews traction and prevent slip-and-falls. It also melts thin ice over time. In Midwest winters this is on the rig year-round because nobody trusts February to skip them.

🧩Parts
  • Bagged salt: 50-lb bags typically.
  • Scoop or spreader: A small hand scoop for spot-application.
🏷️Alternate names

"Ice melt," "rock salt," "traction salt," "calcium chloride" (specific compound), "the salt."

❄️
Rookie Mistake — Forgetting the Salt at Winter ScenesA roadway MVA in January in southern Illinois with black ice underfoot — somebody is going down hard. First five minutes on scene in winter: salt the working area BEFORE the crews start moving heavy gear around. Slip-and-fall injuries on the fireground are a leading cause of lost time.
🐾
Don't Pile It UpSalt works best evenly broadcast. A big pile dumped in one place doesn't melt the area around it. Scoop and spread thin.
2× Bolt Cutters (1 Large, 1 Small)
AKA: Big bolt cutter/small bolt cutter, heavy cutter, medium cutter, long-handled cutter, "the big one" / "the small one"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two bolt cutters carried as a matched pair — a large-frame cutter (typically 24" to 36" handles) for heavy-gauge locks, chains, bolts, padlocks, cable, and metal strapping a smaller cutter can't bite through, and a smaller-frame cutter (previously logged on this rig as the "medium," roughly 18" to 24" handles) for lighter cutting tasks: chain-link fencing, light gauge padlocks, wire, cable, thin rebar. The long handles on the large cutter deliver enormous mechanical advantage. Reach for the small one when the material is clearly going to give; reach for the large one when you're not sure.

🧩Parts
  • Blades / jaws: Hardened steel cutting edges on both. Must be aligned — misaligned blades won't cut cleanly.
  • Blade pivot: Center bolt that holds the jaws together on each cutter.
  • Handles: Long on the large cutter for mechanical advantage; shorter on the small cutter for maneuverability and portability.
  • Springs: Return the handles open after each cut.
🏷️Alternate names

Large: "big cutters," "24-inch cutter," "36-inch cutter," "heavy bolt cutters." Small: "medium cutters" (older logs), "18-inch cutters," "wire cutters" (informal).

🔗
Rookie Mistake — Cutting Hardened Steel Locks With the Wrong CutterHardened-shackle padlocks (Master Lock "shrouded" or "hockey puck" locks) will chip or roll a bolt cutter blade and NOT cut — with either cutter. You'll feel the blade deflect and nothing happens, except now your blade is nicked. For hardened locks: use the rotary saw, angle grinder, or Halligan. Know your target before you pick a tool.
🔀
Right Tool, Right JobThe small cutter won't budge a 5/8" hardened chain. The large cutter is overkill on light wire. Learn to size up the material first. Forcing a too-small cutter bends the blades and takes the tool out of service.
✂️
Keep the Blades OiledDry pivot points and dry blades wear faster and require more force. A drop of oil on the pivot and blade edges after each use keeps both cutters moving smoothly. Blades that are chipped or misaligned need maintenance before they go back in service.
2× Life Safety Rope Bags — 200' (Red & Blue)
AKA: Life safety rope, rescue rope, kernmantle rope, blue bag, "the 200-footer," "the red bag/blue bag"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two 200-foot kernmantle life safety ropes, each in its own color-coded bag (red and blue) so crews can grab a rope fast without rooting through a single bag. Kernmantle construction — braided outer sheath (mantle) over a core (kern) of parallel or braided fibers — provides high strength, low stretch, and abrasion resistance. Used for lowering rescuers, raising patients, securing loads, high-angle operations, and any task where a person's life depends on the rope holding. At 200 feet each, they cover significant vertical distances — multi-story buildings, steep embankments, bridge decks — and having two means a second crew or a backup line is never far away.

🧩Parts
  • Kern (core): Load-bearing fibers inside — twisted, parallel, or braided depending on construction.
  • Mantle (sheath): Woven outer jacket — protects the kern and handles abrasion.
  • Ends / terminations: Factory-finished or field-whipped to prevent fraying.
  • Color-coded bag (red or blue): Stored for rapid deployment without tangles — the color makes it identifiable across the compartment at a glance.
  • Tag/label: Shows rated capacity, length, manufacture date, and inspection history.
🏷️Alternate names

"Life safety rope," "rescue rope," "kernmantle," "technical rope," "the 200," "long rope," "blue bag" / "red bag," "safety bag," "rope bag."

🔎
Inspect Before Every UseRun the rope through your hands before any life-safety application. Feel for sheath abrasion (rough, fuzzy, or cut strands), soft spots (kern damage under intact sheath), stiffness (chemical contamination), or flat sections (shock-loaded). One damaged spot means the rope is OUT OF SERVICE. Life safety rope is retired after any fall arrest or known shock load, period.
☀️
UV, Heat, and Chemicals Degrade RopeNylon and polyester life safety ropes degrade from UV exposure, high heat, and chemical contamination (acids, bases, fuels). Never store in direct sunlight. Keep out of the engine exhaust bay. If a rope contacts an unknown chemical, it's out of service until inspected or condemned.
🎨
Color Coding Exists for a ReasonKnow which bag is which by color — don't mix contents between bags. Arizona Vortex gear has its own blue bag elsewhere on the rig; don't confuse it with this one. The whole point of color coding is quick positive identification under stress. If you can't tell what's in the bag by the color, something went back in the wrong bag.
🪓

Officer's Side Compartment Over Wheel

Pics: Front Pics: Rear
Hand Tools · Forcible Entry · Rigging Kit · Arizona Vortex
Flat Head Axe
AKA: Flat axe, FH axe, marrying axe, "the flat-head"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A fire-service axe with one cutting bit and one flat striking face on the head. The cutting edge chops wood, drywall, doors, and roofing material. The flat striking surface drives a Halligan bar (or any other tool you need to hammer) — this is why it's called a "marrying" axe: it marries up to the Halligan in the universal "irons" set. Single most useful manual tool on the fireground.

🧩Parts
  • Cutting bit / edge: Sharp side. KEEP IT SHARP. A dull axe is dangerous because it deflects.
  • Flat poll / striking face: The opposite side of the head, hardened steel.
  • Head / cheek: The body of the axe.
  • Eye: The hole the handle fits through.
  • Handle / haft: Fiberglass or hickory.
  • Belt swell / throat / grip end: The thicker end of the handle for grip.
🏷️Alternate names

"Flat-head axe," "FH axe," "marrying axe," "irons axe" (when paired with Halligan), "fireman's axe."

🪓
Rookie Mistake — Chopping With a Dull AxeA dull axe glances off and into your shin. Sharp axes bite where you aim them. If the edge has dings, dents, or a rolled bit, take it to be sharpened. Don't swing it. And NEVER use the flat poll to strike anything hardened — you'll mushroom the poll and create dangerous metal burrs.
⚒️
Halligan + Flat-Head = "The Irons"The marriage of Halligan and flat-head axe is the most basic forcible-entry set in the fire service. Probies who can't fluently set the Halligan and drive it with the flat-head are NOT ready for entry. Drill this until you can do it blindfolded.
Pick Axe
AKA: Pickhead axe, PH axe, fire axe, "the pickhead"
+
📖What it is & what it does

An axe with a cutting bit on one side and a SHARP pick (point) on the other. The pick punctures and pulls — great for pulling ceilings, hooking sheet metal, prying roof decking, and overhauling. The cutting bit chops like a regular axe. This is the axe a truck company chief grabs when he doesn't know yet which task he'll need.

🧩Parts
  • Cutting bit / edge.
  • Pick point: The sharp piercing end opposite the bit.
  • Head / cheek.
  • Handle and grip.
🏷️Alternate names

"Pickhead axe," "PH axe," "pick axe," "fire axe," "truckies' axe" (used heavily on truck companies).

🎯
Rookie Mistake — Sheathing the Pick End in a CoatThe pick end is sharp. Probies who clip the axe to their gear or set it loose in a compartment with the pick exposed have stabbed themselves and their crew. Use a sheath. Store it pick-down. Mind the pick end every time you set it down.
🪚
NEVER Strike the Halligan With the Pick EndThe pick is brittle. It'll snap and fly. Only the FLAT-HEAD axe poll strikes the Halligan. Period.
Halligan
AKA: Halligan bar, hooligan tool, the bar, "the Halligan"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The most iconic forcible-entry tool in the American fire service. Forged one-piece bar with a prying adze, a flat forked claw, and a pointed pick at the ends. Used to force doors, windows, locks, padlocks, gas valves, manholes, and just about everything else. Married with the flat-head axe to form "the irons." If you can only have one tool going into a building, this is it.

🧩Parts
  • Adze end (chisel/blade): Wide curved blade for prying doors at the lock side.
  • Pick (point): Sharp point at 90° to the adze — drives into a door at the lock or hinge, drives into lock cylinders.
  • Fork / claws: Two-pronged forked end opposite — pulls hardware, pries doors at the hinge side, gives leverage.
  • Shaft: The main bar, your lever and grip surface.
  • Throat / shoulder: The narrowed area between the head and the shaft.
🏷️Alternate names

"Halligan bar," "Halligan tool," "the bar," "hooligan tool" (alternate spelling, sometimes seen on older training material), "Pro-Bar" (a specific brand).

🚪
Rookie Mistake — Forcing in the Wrong DirectionMost American residential doors open INWARD. You set the Halligan and drive it AGAINST the door swing — the adze goes between door and jamb, bevel toward the lock. Forcing outward on an inward-swinging door bends the metal but won't open the door. Know which way the door swings BEFORE you commit. Hinges visible = door swings toward you (outward). No hinges visible = swings away (inward).
🤝
Two-Person Forcible EntryOne holds the Halligan with both hands, the other strikes the Halligan with the flat-head axe poll. Striker has to communicate — "set," "ready," "STRIKING." Probies who try to do both jobs alone take twice as long and miss strikes. Work as a team.
Sledgehammer
AKA: Sledge, mule, persuader, "the sledge"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A heavy two-handed striking hammer. 8 lb, 10 lb, or 12 lb on most rigs. Drives Halligans into stubborn doors, breaks masonry, pulverizes locks, and applies brute force when finesse has failed. Slower swing than an axe but vastly more striking energy.

🧩Parts
  • Head: Heavy steel block, two flat striking faces.
  • Handle: Long fiberglass or wood haft.
  • Grip: Textured at the swinging end.
🏷️Alternate names

"Sledge," "sledgehammer," "mule," "persuader," "the big hammer."

🦵
Rookie Mistake — Striker Standing in the Wrong SpotWhen two people work the irons and the second is swinging a sledge to drive a Halligan, the Halligan operator's HEAD is right next to the strike zone. Miss-strikes happen. Strikers stand offset, swing controlled, and the Halligan operator's face is positioned AWAY from where the sledge would go if it slips off. Helmets and visors down — always.
🪨
Strike SquareGlancing blows on a Halligan or chisel send the tool flying. Square strikes. Both hands. Controlled arc. This isn't a baseball game.
2× Closet Pikes
AKA: Closet hook, short pike, drywall hook, "the closet pike"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A short-handled pike pole specifically designed for working in tight quarters — closets, bathrooms, tight hallways — where a 6 or 8-foot pike won't swing. Used to pull ceilings, drag burning material out of a void space, and check for fire extension behind walls. Short, vicious, and made for cramped overhaul.

🧩Parts
  • Hook head: Curved pike + flat scraping blade. Pulls and pries.
  • Ferrule: The metal collar where the head meets the handle.
  • Short handle: Typically 2–4 feet.
  • Butt cap: Protects the bottom of the handle and gives a striking surface.
🏷️Alternate names

"Closet hook," "drywall hook," "short pike," "short hook," "Boston rake" (some versions). NY Hook is a different — longer — hook.

⛓️
Rookie Mistake — Yanking Straight DownPulling drywall straight down loads your spine and accomplishes less. Use a sweeping pull — hook into the ceiling and rotate your hips, not your back. Closet pikes are short for a reason; they let you stand close and use leverage, not muscle.
🩸
Don't Pull Onto YourselfWhatever's behind that ceiling — water, plaster, hot embers — is coming DOWN. Helmet flap down, neck protected, head turned away as material falls. Same rule for NY hooks and longer pikes.
Rigging Kit
AKA: Rigging bag, rescue rigging kit, MA kit, "the rigging"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A consolidated bag of rigging hardware used for mechanical advantage systems, load securing, and technical rescue operations. Contains slings, pulleys, carabiners, prusik cords, and related components packaged together so crews can deploy a complete rigging system without hunting across multiple compartments. Replaces the individual sling bag and separate pulley system previously stored in this compartment.

🧩Parts
  • Slings / anchor slings: Load-rated webbing or round slings for anchoring and load wrapping.
  • Pulleys (sheaves): Single and double sheave pulleys for mechanical advantage systems.
  • Locking carabiners: Rated hardware connecting the rigging components.
  • Prusik cords: Short loops used as friction-grab progress capture devices.
  • Rope segments: Any dedicated rigging rope packed with the kit.
  • Rigging bag: The outer container — keeps the entire system organized and deployable.
🏷️Alternate names

"Rigging bag," "rescue rigging kit," "MA kit," "Z-rig kit," "haul kit," "rigging package."

🪢
Know Your Load Path Before You Build ItEvery component in a rigging system is load-bearing. Before you deploy this kit for a life-safety operation, you must be able to trace every connection from anchor to load and verify each piece is correctly oriented and rated. If you can't do that confidently, you support the technician who can — you don't run the rigging alone. This is technician-level work.
🔍
Inspect After Every Use — Repack CorrectlyCarabiners, slings, and prusik cords that get field use need inspection before they go back in the bag. A cracked carabiner, a cut sling, or a heat-damaged prusik cord fails at a fraction of rated load. Repack in the correct configuration so the next crew can deploy it without untangling.
🏷️
Never Remove Tags From ComponentsWorking load limit tags on slings and carabiners are not decorations. They're your only field reference for what the piece is rated to hold. A sling with a missing tag is out of service — you have no way to know if it's been overloaded or what its capacity is.
Arizona Vortex (Blue Bag)
AKA: Vortex, tripod rescue system, confined space frame, "the Vortex"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A modular, aircraft-aluminum multipod anchor system used for confined space entry/rescue and high-angle rope rescue. The Vortex creates a rigging point above a manhole, trench, or window when no overhead anchor exists. Legs extend and lock into an A-frame or tripod configuration. A pulley or mechanical advantage system runs through the apex to raise or lower a rescuer or victim.

🧩Parts
  • Legs (3 or 4): Adjustable aluminum tubes that lock at length.
  • Apex connector: Top junction — all rigging runs through here.
  • Feet / base pads: Spread load and grip the ground.
  • Blue bag: Color-coded storage — blue = Vortex system.
🏷️Alternate names

"Arizona Vortex," "Vortex," "multipod," "tripod," "confined space frame," "the blue bag." The Arizona Vortex brand is made by Rescue Response Gear.

⚠️
Training Required Before UseThe Vortex is a specialized confined space and rope rescue tool. Setting it up wrong — wrong leg angle, apex not plumb, wrong rigging — can collapse the system under load. You need formal confined space rescue training before you touch this on a real incident. Know where it is; leave the rigging to trained personnel until you are trained.
Air Bag Controller
AKA: Airbag controller, pneumatic bag controller, lifting bag controller, "the controller"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The pneumatic control unit that regulates air pressure to high-pressure lifting bags. Connects to an air supply (SCBA cylinder or cascade) and lets you inflate/deflate bags precisely. The controller shows bag pressure and has separate inflate/deflate valves for each bag. Used in vehicle extrication and structural collapse to lift crushing loads off victims.

🧩Parts
  • Inlet fitting: Connects to air supply (SCBA cylinder or cascade system).
  • Pressure gauge: Shows current bag pressure — do not exceed bag's rated max PSI.
  • Inflate/deflate valves: Separate controls for each bag port.
  • Outlet hoses: Run to each individual lifting bag.
🏷️Alternate names

"Airbag controller," "pneumatic bag controller," "lifting bag controller," "bag control unit." Manufacturer varies — Paratech and Holmatro are common brands. Max pressure for most high-pressure bags is 118 PSI.

🎈
Rookie Mistake — Overinflating a BagHigh-pressure lifting bags are rated to a max PSI (usually 118). Over-inflating doesn't lift more — it pops the bag. A bag failure under a 4,000-lb vehicle is catastrophic. Watch the gauge, use cribbing as you go, and never exceed rated pressure. The bag lifts; the cribbing holds.
🧰
