Plasma Torch · PPE · Hand Tools · Toolboxes · Wrenches · Sockets · Cribbing · Ratchet Straps
Toolbox with SAE & Metric Wrenches
AKA: Wrench box, combo wrenches, spanners, "the wrench set"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A toolbox containing combination wrenches in both SAE (inch) and metric sizes. American cars and most domestic structural fittings are SAE; foreign cars, motorcycles, and most modern equipment are metric. Used to remove battery terminals (a HUGE deal on vehicle extrications), break loose bolted assemblies, work on hydraulic fittings, and do any task where an impact gun is too aggressive.

🧩Parts
  • Combination wrench: One end is open-end, the other is box-end (six-point or twelve-point).
  • SAE sizes: Fractional inch (1/4", 5/16", 3/8", 7/16", 1/2", 9/16", 5/8", 11/16", 3/4", 13/16", 7/8", 15/16", 1").
  • Metric sizes: Millimeter (8, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 21, 22, 24).
  • Toolbox / case: Foam-fit cutouts so you can SEE which wrench is missing.
🏷️Alternate names

"Combo wrenches," "combination wrenches," "spanners" (British/Australian), "open-end and box-end wrench."

🔧
Rookie Mistake — Wrong Standard WrenchA 9/16" SAE wrench fits LOOSELY on a 14mm metric nut. The wrench cams off and rounds the corners of the head. Now nobody can get that bolt off. Match the system — SAE on SAE, metric on metric. Vehicle? Look at where it was built. Domestic = usually SAE. European/Asian = usually metric.
🔋
Disconnect the Battery — Negative FirstCritical step for any vehicle extrication. The wrench from THIS box is the one that gets the battery terminal off. Negative terminal first (black, usually 10mm or 13mm), then positive (red). Disconnecting positive first risks an arc-flash short to the chassis if your wrench touches metal. Negative-first is the safe sequence.
Standard Toolbox
AKA: Tool box, general tools, hand tools, "the toolbox"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The "general purpose" toolbox containing pliers, screwdrivers, hammers, channel locks, vise grips, tape measure, utility knife, and the everyday mechanical tools. The Squad turns into a mobile workshop more often than people realize — a single Philips screwdriver can solve a problem that the spreaders can't.

🧩Parts (typical contents)
  • Pliers: Needle-nose, lineman's, slip-joint, channel locks.
  • Vise grips: Locking pliers — saves the day when something is rounded off.
  • Screwdrivers: Phillips and slotted, various sizes.
  • Adjustable wrench: Crescent-style for odd-size fasteners.
  • Tape measure.
  • Utility knife / box cutter.
  • Hammer.
  • Flashlight (in some kits).
🏷️Alternate names

"Tool box," "general tools," "hand tools," "house kit."

🧹
Rookie Mistake — Tools Going Home With YouStandard pliers and screwdrivers walk off. You used them on your truck, you "borrowed" them, you put them in your locker. Now the next crew opens the toolbox and the channel locks are gone. Don't be that guy. Tools stay on the rig. Take ten extra seconds to put it back exactly where it came from.
Socket Sets
AKA: Sockets, ratchet set, socket kit, "the sockets"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A set of ratcheting socket wrenches with multiple drive sizes (1/4", 3/8", 1/2") and a range of socket sizes in both SAE and metric. Used wherever a fastener is recessed, in a tight spot, or needs repeated turns that wrenches can't deliver. Faster than wrenches once you can break the fastener loose.

🧩Parts
  • Ratchet handles: 1/4", 3/8", 1/2" drives.
  • Sockets: Shallow and deep, six-point and twelve-point, SAE and metric.
  • Extensions: Short and long, for reaching recessed fasteners.
  • Universal joints / swivels: For working around corners.
  • Adapters: Step from one drive size to another.
  • Case / foam tray: Foam cutouts show empty spots.
🏷️Alternate names

"Sockets," "ratchet set," "socket wrench," "socket kit."

🔩
Rookie Mistake — Using a Chrome Socket on an Impact GunSame rule as the 1/2" impact. Chrome (shiny) sockets are HAND sockets. They shatter under impact use. Impact-rated sockets are matte black or dark gray. Do not put a chrome socket on the impact wrench. Ever.
📐
Six-Point vs. Twelve-PointSix-point sockets grip the fastener on its FLATS — far less likely to round off a stuck bolt. Twelve-point sockets fit on TWELVE possible positions of the fastener, which is convenient for tight angles but more likely to slip on a rusted fastener. If a nut is rounded or hard to break loose, use a six-point.
More Cribbing & Wedges
AKA: Backup cribbing, supplementary blocks, "the spare cribbing"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Additional cribbing and wedges to back up the supply in the front officer compartment. Big extrications burn through cribbing fast — a four-corner stabilization on a heavy vehicle can use 30+ pieces. The reserve is here so you don't run out at the worst possible moment.

🏷️Alternate names

"Spare cribbing," "backup cribbing," "extra blocks." See OF-03 for the full parts breakdown — same wood, same rules, just more of it.

📦
Rookie Mistake — Pulling From the Reserve When the Front Box is FullThe reserve is the reserve. You pull from the primary stock first. Probies who go to the back compartment for cribbing because it's closer leave the front compartment fully stocked while the reserve runs out, then the next call finds zero spare cribs. Follow the inventory order.
Ratchet Straps
AKA: Ratchet tie-downs, cargo straps, load straps, "the straps"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Heavy-duty ratcheting cargo straps with end hooks. Used to secure loads, anchor stabilization struts, tie down equipment, and rig temporary fastening at scenes. The ratchet mechanism lets you put significant tension on the strap with one hand.

🧩Parts
  • Ratchet handle: The pump lever that takes up slack.
  • Mandrel / drum: The shaft inside the ratchet that winds the strap.
  • Release lever / pawl release: Squeeze to release tension — be careful, it can free-spool fast.
  • Webbing: Color-coded by rating (usually).
  • End hooks: S-hooks, J-hooks, flat hooks, or D-rings depending on type.
  • Working Load Limit (WLL) tag: Sewn on the strap.
🏷️Alternate names

"Ratchet straps," "ratchet tie-downs," "cargo straps," "load straps." Cam-buckle straps are a DIFFERENT, lower-capacity tool.

💥
Rookie Mistake — Releasing a Tensioned Ratchet Strap CarelesslyA loaded ratchet strap stored a lot of energy. Pop the release and the handle flips violently — broken thumbs and split lips happen. Hold the handle as you release; let it unfold under control. And NEVER stand in line with the strap's recoil direction.
📊
Know the RatingA 1" strap holds less than a 2" strap. A 2" strap holds less than a 4" strap. Working Load Limit on the tag is NOT the break strength — it's a working load with safety factor. If a strap looks chewed, frayed, melted, or its tag is gone, out of service.
Plasma Torch IR/UV Safety Glasses
AKA: Plasma safety glasses, cutting glasses, IR/UV glasses, shade glasses
+
📖What it is & what it does

Safety eyewear with lenses rated to filter the infrared and ultraviolet radiation generated by plasma cutting operations. Worn by any bystander or crew member near the plasma arc who is not wearing the full face shield — the face shield protects the operator, but secondary radiation from the arc can reach anyone within line of sight. These glasses give that secondary protection without requiring a full helmet.

🧩Parts
  • Lens: Shade-rated optical lens (typically shade 3–5 for bystander protection).
  • Frame: Wrap-around for side protection.
  • Temples / arms: Keep the glasses seated securely.
🏷️Alternate names

"IR/UV glasses," "plasma safety glasses," "cutting glasses," "shade glasses," "filter glasses."

👁️
Anyone Near the Arc Needs Eye ProtectionThe plasma arc produces intense UV and IR radiation that can damage eyes at distances well beyond the operator. If crew members are working within sight of an active plasma cut, they wear these glasses — no exceptions. Arc eye (photokeratitis) is extremely painful and symptoms are delayed by hours, so you won't know you were exposed until the damage is done.
Welding Gloves
AKA: Leather welding gloves, gauntlets, plasma gloves, "the welding gloves"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Heavy leather gauntlet-style gloves designed to protect the operator's hands and forearms from the heat, sparks, and molten metal spatter produced by plasma cutting. Standard structural firefighting gloves are not adequate for plasma operations — the heat and spatter exposure is sustained and concentrated in a way that exceeds their protection. These stay with the plasma torch and go on before the arc starts.

🧩Parts
  • Palm and back: Heavy split cowhide or chrome-tanned leather.
  • Gauntlet cuff: Extended cuff protects the wrist and lower forearm.
  • Lining (some models): Insulated lining for additional heat protection.
  • Seams: Stitched inside-out so seams don't contact the skin under heat.
🏷️Alternate names

"Welding gloves," "leather gauntlets," "plasma gloves," "cutting gloves."

🔥
Rookie Mistake — Using Structural Gloves for Plasma WorkYour structural firefighting gloves are designed for radiant heat and steam — NOT for direct contact with molten metal spatter and sustained high-temperature exposure at a cutting point. Plasma spatter will burn through a structural glove. Use the welding gloves for cutting operations.
Rescue Blanket
AKA: Emergency blanket, Mylar blanket, space blanket, foil blanket, "the rescue blanket"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A heavy-duty insulating blanket used on rescue scenes to preserve patient body temperature, reduce windchill, and provide minor flame/radiant heat protection during extrication. Different from the foil "space blankets" — a true rescue blanket is heavier, more durable, and reusable. Used to cover patients during long extrications, protect them from sparks during cutting operations, and as a windbreak in field conditions.

🧩Parts
  • Insulating layer: Metallized or foam-backed material that reflects body heat.
  • Outer surface: Durable, tear-resistant facing.
  • Size: Large enough to fully cover a supine adult patient.
🏷️Alternate names

"Emergency blanket," "rescue blanket," "Mylar blanket" (foil type), "space blanket" (the thin disposable version), "thermal blanket."

🌡️
Hypothermia Starts FastA patient lying on cold pavement at a winter MVA scene loses core temperature fast — especially if wet or in shock. Get the rescue blanket UNDER the patient (ground conduction is a major heat loss path) and over them simultaneously. Don't wait until the patient is shivering. Hypothermia impairs clotting — it compounds trauma.
✂️
Protect the Patient From Cutting SparksWhen using the plasma torch, reciprocating saw, or angle grinder near a patient during extrication, the rescue blanket covers the patient to shield from sparks and debris. Weight down the edges so it doesn't blow off in wind.
Wool Blanket
AKA: Wool, wool blanket, fire blanket (informal), "the wool"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A heavy wool blanket used for patient warming at trauma scenes and MVAs. Wool retains insulating properties even when wet — unlike cotton, which collapses and conducts cold as soon as it absorbs moisture. On a wet, cold scene, a wool blanket over a patient buys time against hypothermia. Also provides mild protection from sparks (wool chars rather than melting, unlike synthetics).

🧩Parts
  • Wool body: 100% wool or high-wool-content blend.
  • Size: Large enough for a full patient wrap.
🏷️Alternate names

"Wool blanket," "wool," "patient blanket," "trauma blanket" (informal).

🧼
Wool vs. Synthetic — Know the DifferenceWool chars under flame exposure. Synthetic blankets (nylon, polyester) melt and can adhere to a patient's skin. If sparks are in the area, wool goes on the patient — not a synthetic. After use, wool blankets need to be properly cleaned and dried before restocking.
Metric & Standard Open End Wrenches
AKA: Open end wrenches, combination wrenches, spanners, "the open ends"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A set of open-end wrenches in both metric and SAE (standard/imperial) sizes — stored on the top shelf of the OS Rear compartment for quick access. Open-end wrenches are faster to put on and take off fasteners than box-end wrenches because they don't have to thread over the bolt head — critical in confined spaces where you can only get partial turns. Used for hydraulic fittings, equipment maintenance on scene, and anywhere quick wrench access matters.

🧩Parts
  • Open end: U-shaped jaw that slides onto a fastener from the side.
  • Handle: Allows torque to be applied.
  • Size marking: Stamped on the head — both sides usually different sizes.
  • Set (metric and SAE): Covers the range of fastener sizes you'll encounter on domestic and foreign equipment.
🏷️Alternate names

"Open end wrenches," "combination wrenches" (box end + open end), "spanners" (British/older term), "flat wrenches."

🔧
Open End vs. Box End — Use the Right OneOpen-end wrenches are faster but can slip off a rounded fastener. Box-end wrenches (enclosed, like a ring) grip 6 or 12 points and are less likely to round off a nut. For heavy torque on stubborn fasteners, use the box end. For quick removal in tight spaces, use the open end.
Plasma Torch
AKA: Plasma cutter, plasma arc cutter, plasma cutting tool
+
📖What it is & what it does

A plasma cutter uses a high-velocity jet of ionized gas (plasma) to cut through electrically conductive metals — steel, aluminum, copper. It works by passing an electrical arc through the gas, heating it to plasma state and melting the metal. Capable of cutting sheet metal and structural steel quickly and precisely — far faster than an angle grinder on thin to medium material.

🧩Parts
  • Power unit / inverter: Converts power to the high-frequency arc needed for plasma cutting.
  • Torch / cutting head: Directs the plasma stream to the workpiece.
  • Electrode: Inside the torch — creates the arc. Consumable part.
  • Nozzle / tip: Shapes the plasma stream. Consumable — must be inspected regularly.
  • Air/gas supply line: Provides the ionized gas (usually compressed air).
  • Ground clamp / work lead: Completes the electrical circuit through the workpiece.
  • Trigger / cutting trigger: Initiates the arc and plasma flow.
🏷️Alternate names

"Plasma arc cutter," "plasma torch," "plasma cutting tool," "plasma rig."

⚡
CRITICAL SAFETY — Arc Flash and UV RadiationThe plasma arc generates intense UV and infrared radiation. NEVER operate without the plasma cutter face protector — even brief unprotected exposure can cause arc eye (photokeratitis) and severe skin burns. Arc flash injuries happen in fractions of a second. Face protector on before the arc starts, every time.
🔥
Molten Metal SpatterPlasma cutting produces a spray of molten metal and sparks. Clear the work area of bystanders and flammable materials before cutting. The spatter travels farther than you expect — a full 6-foot radius at minimum. Keep fire watch during and after cutting operations.
⚡
Rookie Mistake — Cutting Near Energized LinesPlasma cutters only work on conductive materials, but the metal you're cutting may be in contact with energized electrical systems — vehicles, structural components, machinery. Confirm electrical isolation or de-energization before cutting. Cutting through an energized conductor can be fatal.
Plasma Torch Face Shield
AKA: Welding shield, cutting helmet, plasma face shield, auto-darkening helmet
+
📖What it is & what it does

A face shield or welding helmet rated for plasma cutting operations, providing full-face protection from UV/IR radiation, arc flash, and molten metal spatter. Must be rated at the appropriate shade level for plasma cutting — typically shade 8–10 depending on amperage. Stored with the plasma cutter and NEVER used without it.

🧩Parts
  • Outer shell / body: Protects from heat and spatter.
  • Filter lens / shade lens: The darkened optical lens that filters UV and IR. Must be the correct shade for plasma cutting (typically shade 8–10).
  • Clear cover lens: Protects the filter lens from spatter — inspect before each use, replace when obscured.
  • Headband / suspension: Adjustable harness that holds the shield to the head.
  • Lift mechanism (flip-front models): Allows the operator to raise the shield without removing it.
👁️
Never Operate the Plasma Cutter Without This ShieldArc eye from unprotected plasma exposure causes intense pain, photosensitivity, and temporary vision loss within hours of exposure — often after you've finished cutting and feel fine. Symptoms are delayed. The only protection is not getting exposed in the first place. Shield on, arc starts. Non-negotiable.
📦

Rear of Squad Compartment — "The Big Stuff"

Pics: Top Shelf Pics: Second Shelf Pics: Left Vertical Pics: Middle Vertical Pics: Right Vertical Pics: Bottom Shelf
Air Bags · Extinguishers · Stokes · NY Hooks · Pike Poles · Smoke Ejectors · Dewalt Batteries
Multi-lift Air Bags (5 Total)
AKA: Lifting bags, high-pressure airbags, rescue bags, Vetter bags, "the lifting bags"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Five Multi-lift high-pressure lifting air bags stored in the rear compartment across two shelves: 3 bags (1 small, 2 medium) on the second shelf, and 2 large bags on the middle vertical shelf. Inflate between a load and the ground to lift heavy objects: vehicles off victims, collapsed structural members, industrial equipment. Capable of lifting tens of thousands of pounds (each bag rated individually). Used with the dedicated Air Bag Controller in Dewalt bag stored on the bottom shelf.

🧩Parts
  • Second Shelf — 3 bags (1 small, 2 medium): Smaller Multi-lift bags for tighter void spaces and supplemental lifts.
  • Middle Vertical Shelf — 2 large bags: High-capacity lifters for heavy structural loads.
  • Working hoses: Color-coded hoses connecting bags to controller.
  • Quick-connect couplers: Must FULLY click into place — partial seating leaks pressure.
  • Bag ratings: Each bag labeled with rated capacity and max lift height — READ before use.
🏷️Alternate names

"Multi-Lift bags," "high-pressure airbags," "lifting bags," "rescue bags," "Vetter bags" (brand), "Paratech bags" (brand), "HP bags."

📐
Rookie Mistake — Inflating Without CribbingAn airbag is a TEMPORARY lifter. Once the load is up, you crib UNDER the load. Then deflate. NEVER trust the bag alone. Bags slip, rotate, and can fail. Lift an inch, crib an inch — every single time.
🪨
Stack Big on BottomIn a two-bag stack (snowman), the BIGGER bag goes on the BOTTOM. Inflate bottom first, then top. Reversing this causes the stack to walk out from under the load. This principle has gotten people hurt for decades. Non-negotiable.
⚖️
Center the Bag on the LoadBag off-center makes the load tilt. Match the bag to the contact surface and center it on the lift point before inflating.
Air Bag Controller (Dewalt Bag)
AKA: Multi-Lift controller, bag controller, airbag controller, "the controller"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The dedicated controller for the Multi-lift high-pressure air bag system, stored in a yellow Dewalt bag on the bottom shelf of the rear compartment. Regulates supply pressure from the cascade or SCBA bottle down to working pressure and allows independent control of two bags via dead-man valves. This is the MODERN controller — it goes with the Multi-lift bags stored on this compartment's shelves, NOT with the older-generation bags whose controller lives on the officer's traverse.

🧩Parts
  • Supply inlet: High-pressure fitting from cascade or SCBA cylinder.
  • Pressure regulator: Steps down to bag working pressure.
  • Supply gauge & bag pressure gauges: One per channel.
  • Dual dead-man controls: Inflate/deflate lever per bag — release = bag holds pressure.
  • Color-coded working hoses: One per bag outlet.
  • Dewalt bag (yellow): Protects and organizes the controller and hoses.
🏷️Alternate names

"Multi-Lift controller," "bag controller," "airbag controller," "the Dewalt bag controller."

🔀
Two Controllers on This Rig — Match Them CorrectlyThis Dewalt-bag controller is for the Multi-lift bags in the rear. The older controller on the officer's traverse is for the older-generation bags. They have DIFFERENT working pressures. Using this controller on the old bags will over-pressurize and rupture them. The Dewalt bag controller stays with the Multi-lift system only.
Multi-force Air Bag (Snowman)
AKA: Snowman bag, stacked bag, multi-force system, double-bag stack
+
📖What it is & what it does

A two-bag stacked air bag configuration — one bag on top of another — used when you need more vertical lift height than a single bag provides. Called "snowman" because two stacked bags resemble a snowman's body in profile. Used when the void space is too shallow for a single large bag but significant vertical travel is needed. Operates with the Air Bag Controller in Dewalt bag. Stored on the bottom shelf of the rear compartment.

🧩Parts
  • Two bags: Larger on the bottom, smaller on top.
  • Controller: Air Bag Controller in Dewalt bag.
  • Working hoses: Color-coded to each bag.
  • Cribbing: Essential — placed under the load continuously as the stack lifts.
🏷️Alternate names

"Snowman" (universal informal name on scene), "stacked bags," "multi-force bag," "double-stack."

📐
Big Bag on Bottom — No ExceptionsLarger bag ALWAYS on the bottom. Inflate bottom first, completely, then start the top. Reversing this causes the stack to walk out from under the load. A walking bag drops the load on the victim and the rescuers.
🦺
Crib as You Go — Never Trust the Bags AloneLift an inch, crib an inch. Bags are temporary. If one lets go mid-lift with no cribbing, the load drops instantly onto whatever — or whoever — is underneath.
3× Fire Extinguishers (ABC · CO2 · Silver Bullet)
AKA: Extinguishers, cans, dry chem, CO2, water, "the cans"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Three fire extinguishers stored on the left vertical shelf of the rear compartment, each with a different agent type for different fire classes. Know which is which before you grab one — wrong agent on the wrong fire can make things worse.

🧩The Three Extinguishers
  • ABC Dry Chemical: Handles Class A (ordinary combustibles), B (flammable liquids), and C (energized electrical). The all-purpose choice. Leaves a residue.
  • CO2 (Carbon Dioxide): Handles Class B and C fires. Leaves NO residue — preferred for electronics and sensitive equipment. Short effective range. Displaces oxygen, so use in ventilated areas.
  • Silver Bullet (Pressurized Water): Handles Class A fires (ordinary combustibles — wood, paper, fabric). Pressurized water extinguisher. NOT for flammable liquids (Class B) or energized electrical (Class C). The silver canister makes it visually distinct.
🏷️Alternate names

ABC: "dry chem," "ABC can," "purple K" (different agent — don't confuse). CO2: "CO2 can," "carbon dioxide." Silver Bullet: "water extinguisher," "pressurized water," "the silver one."

💧
Rookie Mistake — Water on a Class B or C FireThe Silver Bullet is pressurized water. Water on a gasoline pool fire scatters the fuel and spreads the fire. Water on energized electrical equipment conducts current back to you. READ THE LABEL on each extinguisher. Know which is which at a glance BEFORE you're on scene.
🅿️
P.A.S.S.Pull pin · Aim at the base of the fire · Squeeze handle · Sweep side to side. Aim at the BASE — not the flames. Probies aim at the flames and watch the fire reignite from the unattacked base.
Stokes Basket
AKA: Stokes, rescue basket, basket litter, "the Stokes"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A rigid wire or plastic basket-style patient litter used for moving patients over rough terrain, through tight spaces, up/down rope rescue, off rooftops, and out of basements where a flat backboard can't go. The patient is strapped in and the basket is the package — multiple rescuers carry it or it's rigged for hoist. Stored on the top shelf of the rear compartment.

🧩Parts
  • Basket / shell: Wire-cage or rotomolded plastic body.
  • Rails / runners: Reinforced frame for carrying.
  • Tie-down straps / spider: Multi-point harness over the patient.
  • Attachment points: Rated rigging points for rope work.
  • Foot plate: Solid bottom at the foot end — patient can't slide out.
🏷️Alternate names

"Stokes" (most common), "Stokes basket," "rescue basket," "basket litter," "Junkin basket."

👋
Rookie Mistake — Patient Not Properly StrappedA loosely strapped patient WILL slide out the moment you tip the basket. Cross-strap pattern, snug, with a foot stop. Verify head-to-toe before you lift. If the patient is unconscious, check the straps TWICE.
Fire Investigation Rake
AKA: Debris rake, char rake, overhaul rake, investigator's rake
+
📖What it is & what it does

A specialty rake used by the Fire Investigator during cause-and-origin work to carefully move and sift through char debris without destroying burn patterns and physical evidence. Used for layer-by-layer excavation of a fire scene. Stored on the top shelf alongside the Stokes Basket.

🧩Parts
  • Head with tines: Metal teeth that comb through debris.
  • Handle.
  • Sometimes a flat blade edge on the back.
🏷️Alternate names

"Investigation rake," "char rake," "debris rake," "overhaul rake."

🔍
Rookie Mistake — Raking Before Investigator Releases the SceneIf the investigator hasn't released the scene, raking is THEIR job, not yours. Probies who decide to "help overhaul" while a cause-and-origin investigation is active have ruined prosecutions. When investigation is happening, you support — you don't rake.
NY Hooks & Pike Poles (4 Total)
AKA: Pikes, hooks, NY hooks, ceiling hooks, "the pike poles"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Four long-handled hooks and poles stored on the top shelf for pulling ceilings, dragging burning debris, checking for fire extension, and breaching walls. Two 8-foot New York hooks, one 6-foot New York hook, and one 6-foot pike pole give size options for different situations. The NY hook has a distinct curved blade-and-pike pattern designed for tougher plaster ceilings. The pike pole has a standard pointed pike and curved hook.

🧩What's in this group
  • 2× 8' New York Hooks: Primary overhaul tools for larger rooms and high ceilings.
  • 1× 6' New York Hook: Shorter — better for lower ceilings and tighter spaces.
  • 1× 6' Pike Pole: Standard pike-and-hook head for general pulling and breaching work.
  • All handles: Fiberglass preferred — non-conductive around energized lines.
🏷️Alternate names

"NY hook," "New York hook," "San Francisco hook," "Boston rake," "ceiling hook," "pike pole," "hook" (generic).

⚡
Rookie Mistake — Pole Contacting Energized Service DropEight-foot poles reach the electrical service drop. Wood and aluminum handles conduct electricity. Even fiberglass in wet conditions can carry current. ALWAYS look UP before swinging a long pole near a structure. Probies have been electrocuted by a single careless lift.
🩹
Pull on a Diagonal — Away From Your HeadHook the ceiling and pull on a downward diagonal away from your face. Stand to the SIDE of the area you're pulling. Stuff falls — insulation, hot embers, water, plaster. None of it on your face.
2× Battery-Powered Smoke Ejectors
AKA: Smoke ejectors, ventilation fans, smoke fans, "the smoke ejectors"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two battery-powered smoke ejectors stored on the right vertical shelf of the rear compartment. Used for negative-pressure ventilation — set up in a window or doorway to PULL smoke OUT of a structure. Battery-powered means no cord management and no GFCI dependency — deploy faster and in locations where a generator or building power isn't available. Contrast with PPV (Positive Pressure Ventilation) fans which push air in; ejectors pull smoke out.

🧩Parts
  • Frame / housing: Steel cage around the fan.
  • Fan blade: Large diameter behind protective mesh.
  • Battery pack: Rechargeable — verify charge pre-shift.
  • Mounting hooks / hangers: Hang in a window opening.
  • Stand or legs (some models): Floor-stand operation.
  • Speed control (some models).
🏷️Alternate names

"Smoke ejector," "ventilation fan," "negative-pressure fan," "smoke fan." NOT a PPV fan.

🔋
Check the Battery Pre-ShiftA dead battery on a smoke ejector means manual ventilation in a smoke-filled building. Charge both units every shift. If a battery is swollen or won't hold a charge, it's out of service.
🌬️
Rookie Mistake — Setting Up Ventilation Without Coordinating With AttackVentilation without coordination with the engine company can pull smoke and heat over the attack crew, or feed fresh air to a hidden fire that flashes. Ventilation is coordinated with attack. Talk on the radio. Confirm with the IC.
Umbrella
AKA: Scene umbrella, rain umbrella, "the umbrella"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A scene umbrella stored on the top shelf of the rear compartment. Used at patient contact scenes and long extrications to shield a patient (or crew) from rain, direct sun, or wind during prolonged outdoor operations. Keeping a patient dry and out of the elements during a long extrication reduces heat loss and improves comfort — both of which matter for patient outcomes, especially in trauma.

🧩Parts
  • Canopy: Large coverage area.
  • Shaft / pole: May have a spike or stand for hands-free positioning.
  • Handle.
🌧️
Use It — Don't Forget It's ThereThe umbrella gets overlooked because nobody thinks to grab it. A patient pinned in a car in a rainstorm getting soaked for 25 minutes is a hypothermia risk on top of their trauma. Umbrella out early, over the patient. It's a small thing that matters a lot.
Towel
AKA: Shop towel, rag, wipe-down cloth, "the towel"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A utility towel kept on the left vertical shelf of the rear compartment for wiping down equipment, cleaning fittings before connection, drying hands, and general utility work. Not for patient care — a dedicated first aid/patient towel belongs with EMS supplies. This towel is a tool towel: it lives with the equipment and serves equipment purposes.

🏷️
Don't Cross-ContaminateThe tool towel lives in the rear compartment with equipment. It doesn't go near patients. Keep tool towels and patient-care materials separated.
B-Post Covers
AKA: B-pillar covers, post protectors, side-curtain covers, "B-post covers"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Protective covers placed over vehicle B-posts (the vertical structural pillar between front and rear doors) before the Hurst tools cut through or near the post. B-posts often contain side-curtain airbag gas generators and inflators. The covers protect the patient and rescuers from debris, inadvertent airbag deployment, and sharp edges created by cutting operations. Standard practice in vehicle extrication before any cut near the B-post area.

🧩Parts
  • Cover body: Padded or reinforced material that wraps the B-post.
  • Attachment system: Velcro, straps, or hooks to secure the cover to the post.
🏷️Alternate names

"B-pillar covers," "post covers," "side-curtain covers," "B-post protectors."

💥
Undeployed Airbags Are Live ExplosivesA vehicle in a crash may have undeployed side-curtain airbags stored in the B-post roofline. An unintentional deployment during extrication can strike a rescuer or the patient with enough force to cause serious injury. B-post covers reduce this risk. Always identify potential airbag locations before cutting. If in doubt, cover it.
6-Pack Dewalt Batteries
AKA: Dewalt batteries, power tool batteries, battery pack, "the Dewalts"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A six-pack of Dewalt 20V batteries stored on the bottom shelf of the rear compartment. Powers the battery-powered Dewalt tools on the rig — impact wrenches, saws, and the smoke ejectors. Six packs means capacity for extended operations without waiting on recharging. Cross-compatible with Dewalt 20V MAX platform tools. The chargers live in the cab (3 Dewalt chargers).

🧩Parts
  • 6× Dewalt 20V battery packs: Lithium-ion cells in a hard plastic housing.
  • Charge indicator (some packs): Button-press LED gauge on the pack.
  • Contact terminals: Gold-plated spring contacts — keep clean and dry.
🏷️Alternate names

"Dewalt batteries," "20V packs," "battery pack," "the Dewalts," "power pack."

🔋
Rotate Batteries — Don't Let Them Sit DeadA lithium-ion battery that sits at zero percent for weeks suffers irreversible capacity loss. After every use, packs go to the charger. Check the charge state on arrival at a scene — if the pack is dead, swap it before the tool fails mid-operation. Swap, don't wait.
🌡️
Extreme Heat Degrades Lithium BatteriesPacks stored in a hot compartment in summer lose capacity faster. A swollen pack is a fire hazard — take it out of service immediately and dispose of it properly. Never store a swollen battery on the rig.
🛢️

Officer Coffin Compartment (Top) — Spill Gear

Pics
Pads · Oil Dry · Spill Kit · Oil Pan · Shovels
Absorbent Pads
AKA: Oil pads, sorbent pads, pig pads, "the pads"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Hydrophobic absorbent mats and pads — typically white polypropylene fiber — that absorb oils, fuels, and other hydrocarbons but REJECT water. Drop them on a fuel spill on water and they pull only the fuel. Used at MVA scenes for fuel leak containment, in mechanical rooms after equipment failures, and any hydrocarbon spill where you don't want water-mixed waste.

🧩Parts
  • Sheets or rolls: Pre-cut squares or perforated rolls.
  • Pillows or socks: Cylindrical absorbent for booming off a leak.
  • Color coding: White = oil/fuel only. Gray = universal. Yellow = chemicals.
🏷️Alternate names

"Oil pads," "sorbent pads," "pig pads" (New Pig brand), "fuel pads," "absorbent socks/pillows."

🔥
Rookie Mistake — Fuel-Soaked Pads Are a Fire HazardA pile of gas-soaked pads in a sealed bag in 90° weather is a spontaneous combustion incident waiting to happen. Bag used pads, get them OFF the rig, transfer to hazmat disposal. Never leave used pads stored in the apparatus compartment.
Oil Dry (Top Compartment)
AKA: Speedy Dry, absorbent, "the back-up Speedy Dry"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Backup supply of granular absorbent in the top officer coffin. Same as OF-04 — granular clay-based absorbent for spills. Stored here so the spill kit area has its own reserve.

🏷️Alternate names

"Speedy Dry," "absorbent," "Oil-Dri."

🔄
Refer to OF-04Same parts, same use, same rookie mistakes (storm drain, sweeping too early). Read that entry — don't re-learn it.
Spill Kit
AKA: Hazmat kit, spill response kit, leak kit, "the spill kit"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A self-contained kit for an initial response to a small fuel/oil leak — typically a duffel or hard case holding pads, socks, pillows, disposable bags, gloves, PPE, drain covers, and a basic plug. Used for incidents like a fuel-line cut at an MVA, a leaking ATV, or a small drum leak — anything that's NOT a full-scale hazmat response. For real hazmat, this is initial control only until the hazmat team arrives.

🧩Parts
  • Sorbent pads, socks, pillows.
  • Drain covers / plugs: Cover the storm drain BEFORE the spill reaches it.
  • Non-sparking shovel / scoop.
  • Disposal bags & ties.
  • Nitrile/chemical-resistant gloves.
  • Goggles.
  • Sometimes a pipe-clamping or leak-sealing patch kit.
  • Inventory checklist: Pre-shift verification.
🏷️Alternate names

"Spill kit," "spill response kit," "leak kit," "Class B kit" (informal), "drum kit." Hazmat is a different specialty — this is for small spills only.

🧪
Rookie Mistake — Treating Hazmat Like a SpillThis kit handles fuel and oil. NOT chlorine, NOT anhydrous ammonia, NOT unknown chemicals from an industrial site. Approaching an unidentified leak with just this kit can kill you. If you don't KNOW what it is, treat it as hazmat — back out, isolate, deny entry, call hazmat. Then use this kit for your OWN diesel leaks.
🕳️
Cover Drains EARLYThe single most valuable thing in this kit is the drain cover. Use it FIRST, before the leak migrates. Once a fuel spill hits the storm drain, you have an environmental incident on your hands and your department pays for the cleanup.
Oil Pan
AKA: Drip pan, catch pan, drain pan, "the pan"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A shallow metal or plastic pan that slides UNDER a leaking vehicle or container to catch the dripping fluid. Used at MVAs with active fuel leaks — slide the pan under, contain the fluid, transfer to a sealed container, dispose properly. Stops a small leak from becoming a roadway-wide spill.

🧩Parts
  • Pan body: Wide, shallow.
  • Spout (some models): Pour into a container without spilling.
  • Handles.
🏷️Alternate names

"Drip pan," "catch pan," "drain pan."

🚰
Rookie Mistake — Pan Too Small for the Leak RateA small fuel-line tear leaks fast. A 1-gallon pan overflows in two minutes. Match the pan to the source, plan to transfer the contents to a larger sealed container, and have a backup plan if the leak is bigger than expected.
Shovels
AKA: Spades, scoops, snow shovels, "the shovels"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Standard shovels used to scoop up saturated absorbent for spill disposal, dig out a stuck vehicle, move debris, clear snow at scene access points, and any task where you need to move material by hand. Multiple types may be present — flat (square-point) for scooping, pointed (round-point) for digging.

🧩Parts
  • Blade / scoop: Flat or pointed.
  • Shank: The angled steel between handle and blade.
  • Handle: Wood or fiberglass, with D-grip or straight handle.
🏷️Alternate names

"Spade" (specifically pointed/digging), "scoop shovel" (specifically flat/scooping), "snow shovel," "grain scoop."

🩹
Rookie Mistake — Shovel Used on Hazmat SparksStandard steel shovels create sparks when they hit asphalt or rocks. Fuel-soaked absorbent + sparks = bad day. Use non-sparking shovels (typically aluminum or brass) when scooping up flammable absorbent. Check the spill kit for the non-sparking shovel.
🌊

Driver Coffin Compartment — Water Rescue Gear

Pics
Mustang Suits · Horse Collars · Helmets · Throw Bags · PFDs · Pipe Plugs
2× Mustang Suits
AKA: Mustangs, dry suits, ice rescue suits, immersion suits, "the Mustangs"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Full-body water rescue / cold-water immersion suits — Mustang Survival is the dominant brand, so they're "Mustangs" universally. Provides thermal insulation and (depending on model) inherent flotation when entering cold water — ice rescues, flood rescues, swift water response. Rescuers wearing these can survive in cold water long enough to deploy and retrieve a victim.

🧩Parts
  • Outer shell: Waterproof urethane/Cordura.
  • Inner insulation: Closed-cell foam or fleece liner.
  • Neck and wrist seals: Latex or neoprene gaskets — KEEP WATER OUT.
  • Front zipper: Heavy-duty waterproof zipper. Lube it. Don't yank it dry.
  • Integrated boots / foot pockets.
  • Built-in inherent flotation: Some models. NOT a substitute for a PFD on top.
  • Strobe/light attachment loops.
🏷️Alternate names

"Mustang suits," "Mustangs," "ice rescue suits," "dry suits," "immersion suits," "Gumby suits" (informal — refers to the orange flotation style).

🥶
Rookie Mistake — Getting in the Water Without Cold-Water Rescue TrainingYou don't put on a Mustang and jump in. Cold-water and ice rescue is a specialty technician discipline. Ice shelves break. Currents pull. Hypothermia disables a swimmer in minutes. If you're not trained, you tend the line from shore — you don't enter the water. Period.
🤿
Seals Compromised = Suit UselessDamaged neck/wrist seals let frigid water in. The suit becomes 200 pounds of soaked nylon and you drown. Inspect seals before donning. Tears or cracks = out of service.
2× Horse Collars with Water Rescue Rope
AKA: Horse collar, rescue collar, ring buoy harness, "the collars"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A horseshoe-shaped flotation collar that goes over a victim's head and under their arms — the rescuer reaches out, slips the collar over the victim, and the shore team pulls the rope to retrieve them. Used when the victim is conscious and can lift their arms. The water rescue rope attached lets shore-based rescuers pull the collared victim back to shore without entering the water.

🧩Parts
  • Foam horse-collar body: Floats AND keeps the victim's airway above water.
  • Attachment point: Connected to water rescue rope.
  • Water rescue rope: Floating polypropylene rope, typically bright yellow or orange.
  • Bag / stowage: Pre-coiled in a deployable bag.
🏷️Alternate names

"Horse collar," "rescue collar," "buoy collar," "Carlson collar." Distinct from a ring buoy (which is a hard donut shape).

🪢
Rookie Mistake — Throwing the Bag Like a FootballThrow bags work because the rope feeds OUT of the bag as it flies. Holding the rope-end and throwing the bag underhand lets the rope feed out cleanly. Throwing it overhand or letting go of the rope-end gives a rope that drops in the water at the rescuer's feet. Practice the throw in calm water before you NEED the skill.
🪦
Don't Get Pulled InBracing yourself on the shore when a 200-lb victim is being pulled by current — they pull harder than you. Anchor your line, take a hip-belay or wrap, brace yourself. Probies have been dragged into the water by a panicked victim pulling on the rope.
2× Helmets (Water Rescue)
AKA: Water rescue helmets, swift water helmets, paddling helmets, "the water helmets"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Lightweight, drainable helmets designed for water rescue work. Protects against debris strikes (the deadliest hazard in swift water is being slammed into objects), submerged hazards, and the rope-and-strut work happening above the water. Different from a structural firefighting helmet — water helmets drain, fit under a Mustang hood, and don't trap water.

🧩Parts
  • Outer shell: Plastic or composite, with drainage holes.
  • Suspension / liner.
  • Chin strap: Quick-release buckle.
  • Ear protection (open or closed): Open ears for hearing, closed for impact.
🏷️Alternate names

"Water rescue helmet," "swift water helmet," "paddling helmet," "kayaking helmet." DO NOT use structural firefighting helmets in water — they're too heavy and don't drain.

🚫
Rookie Mistake — Wearing the Wrong HelmetA leather or composite structural helmet in water fills with water and acts as a drag bucket on your head and neck. Use water rescue helmets for water rescue. Wear them BEFORE you approach the water, not after you're standing knee-deep.
2× Throw Bags
AKA: Throw rope, throwing bag, rescue rope bag, "the throw bag"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A bag containing 50–75 feet of floating polypropylene rope, with a foam or buoyant insert. Used for shore-based water rescue — throw the bag past a conscious in-water victim, they grab the rope, you reel them to shore. The bag is the throwing weight; the rope feeds out as it flies. Faster, simpler, and safer than entering the water.

🧩Parts
  • Bag (foam-stiffened): Holds the rope coiled neatly, floats.
  • 50–75 ft floating polypropylene rope: Bright color, water-resistant.
  • Drawstring / closure: Loose enough to feed, tight enough to hold.
  • End knot or loop: The end the rescuer holds.
🏷️Alternate names

"Throw bag," "throw rope," "rescue rope bag." Sometimes confused with a "rescue rope" generally — this specific tool is the bag-deployed throwing rope.

🪢
Rookie Mistake — Tying Yourself Off to the RopeNEVER tie the throw bag rope around your wrist or waist. If the victim panics and pulls, OR if the rope snags on submerged debris, you can be pulled under water and drown. Hold the rope-end in your HAND so you can release it instantly. Loose. Free. Releasable.
🎯
Throw PAST, Not ATThe victim is moving (current). Throw the bag PAST and BEYOND the victim so the rope falls across them. They grab the rope, not the bag. Aim past, not direct.
4× PFDs (Personal Flotation Devices)
AKA: Life vests, life jackets, life preservers, "the vests"
+
📖What it is & what it does

USCG-rated personal flotation devices. Worn by ANY rescuer working near water, by victims being recovered, and by any non-swimmer crew member on a water-side scene. Even competent swimmers wear PFDs in rescue — gear is heavy and exhausting cold water can kill a strong swimmer fast.

🧩Parts
  • Foam panels: Inherent buoyancy — no inflation required.
  • Outer shell: Tough nylon.
  • Side straps and chest strap: Adjust to fit snugly.
  • Front zipper or pull-over design.
  • Whistle attachment: Some PFDs include or accept a rescue whistle.
  • USCG Type: Type III (general boating) or Type V (rescue-rated) is typical. Look at the label.
🏷️Alternate names

"PFD," "life vest," "life jacket," "life preserver," "Mae West" (older slang for inflatable types).

🌊
Rookie Mistake — Loose PFD Floats Off Your BodyA PFD too big or with loose straps will ride UP over the victim's head when they fall in the water — the float keeps the vest at the surface, the person goes UNDER. SNUG the straps. Test with a tug-up — the vest should not slide above the chin.
🦺
Wear It BEFORE You Get to WaterPutting on a PFD after you've slipped into the water is much harder. Don it before you approach the water's edge.
Box with Pipe Plugs
AKA: Pipe plugs, drain plugs, leak plugs, "the pipe plug box"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A box containing assorted plugs and patches for sealing breached pipes, leaking drums, ruptured tanks, and storm drain inlets. Used in hazmat initial response, water main breaks (sometimes), pool drain access, and any leaking pipe where stopping the flow buys time. The kit usually contains conical wooden plugs, inflatable pipe bags, expanding plugs, and rubber patches.

🧩Parts
  • Wooden plugs: Tapered cones in graduated sizes — hammer into a leak.
  • Expanding plugs: Threaded with rubber gasket — twist the wing nut, the rubber expands.
  • Inflatable pipe bags: Insert and inflate to seal larger pipes.
  • Rubber patches: Cover a hole, secured with straps.
  • Wedges & clamps.
🏷️Alternate names

"Pipe plugs," "drain plugs," "Conex plugs" (a type), "tapered plugs," "wooden plugs," "leak kit."

💧
Rookie Mistake — Hammering a Plug into a Pressurized LineA high-pressure pipe will spit your plug back out and hit you with a high-velocity wooden missile. Reduce upstream pressure if possible. Approach from the side, not the direct outflow. And NEVER plug a line you don't know the contents of — sealed pressure in a hazmat line is more dangerous than the leak.
🚐

Cab and EMS Compartment

Pics: Rear Pics: Front
Chargers · Hotstick · Gas Trac · 4-Gas · AED · SCBA Masks · Box Lights · Passport · TIC · Flares
3× Dewalt Battery Chargers
AKA: Dewalt chargers, tool chargers, 20V chargers, "the Dewalt chargers"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Three Dewalt 20V MAX battery chargers in the rear of the cab. Charge the six Dewalt packs stored in the rear compartment — two packs per charger means the whole bank cycles faster. Plugged in at the station between runs.

🧩Parts
  • Charger dock: Dewalt 20V MAX compatible.
  • Charge indicator: Red = charging, green = charged.
  • Power cord.
🔋
Rookie Mistake — Leaving Batteries Off the ChargerTools that come back from a run with dead packs and don't go straight to the charger leave the next crew with dead tools at a scene. Dead batteries go on the charger the moment the rig returns to quarters.
3× Hurst Battery Chargers
AKA: Hurst chargers, eDRAULIC chargers, "the Hurst chargers"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Three Hurst eDRAULIC battery chargers for the Hurst battery-powered rescue tools — cutter, spreader, and ram. These are dedicated Hurst packs; NOT the same as Dewalt. Three chargers keeps all Hurst tool batteries cycling back to full between runs.

🧩Parts
  • Charger body: Hurst-specific dock — only accepts Hurst eDRAULIC packs.
  • Charge status indicator.
  • Power cord.
🔀
Hurst and Dewalt Chargers Are NOT InterchangeableDifferent battery systems entirely. Never force a Hurst pack onto a Dewalt charger or vice versa — you will damage both.
🛠️
Verify Hurst Battery Charge Every Rig CheckThe Hurst tools are your primary extrication system. If the batteries aren't charged, the cutter, spreader, and ram don't work. Check battery state every shift — not just "is the tool there" but "is it ready."
Hotstick
AKA: Volt stick, high-voltage detector, proximity voltage detector, "the hot stick"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A telescoping insulated pole with a voltage-detection tip — wave it near a power line, downed wire, or transformer and it tells you (audibly or by light) if the conductor is energized. Used at MVA scenes involving downed lines or electrical incidents, before anyone gets near a suspected energized conductor.

🧩Parts
  • Insulated fiberglass pole: Telescoping, rated for high-voltage proximity.
  • Sensor tip.
  • LED / audible indicator.
  • Self-test button: ALWAYS verify before use.
🏷️Alternate names

"Hot stick," "voltage stick," "Tic Tracer" (brand), "proximity voltage tester."

⚡
Rookie Mistake — Trusting a Negative Read Without Self-TestA dead battery reads NEGATIVE on a hot wire. Self-test on a known energized source first, test the unknown, re-test the known. Three-step. Every time.
🪦
Hot Wire = 50-Foot MinimumIf it reads energized: don't touch it, don't move it. 50 feet back, call the power company, wait. Downed power lines have killed firefighters.
Gas Trac
AKA: Gas Track, tracking gas detector, leak detector, gas tracker, "the Gas Trac"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A combustible-gas leak detector designed to TRACE a leak back to its source. Different from the 4-gas — the Gas Trac has a flexible probe and sensitivity adjustment to follow a concentration trail to the origin. Used on natural gas calls, propane leaks, and locating the source of a fuel smell.

🧩Parts
  • Detector body.
  • Probe / wand: Long flexible probe sniffs at ground level and around fittings.
  • Display / audible alarm: Rising tone as concentration increases.
  • Sensitivity adjustment.
🏷️Alternate names

"Gas Track," "Gas Trac," "leak detector," "gas tracker," "gas sniffer."

🔥
Rookie Mistake — Gas Trac Is Not a 4-GasThe Gas Trac traces a source. It does NOT replace a 4-gas for confined space entry — no O2, H2S, or CO readout. Two different tools. Don't go into a basement on a gas call with only a Gas Trac.
4-Gas Detectors and Wand (4×)
AKA: 4-gas, multi-gas, atmospheric monitor, "the 4-gas"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Four 4-gas atmospheric monitors with sampling wands. Reads O₂, CO, H₂S, and LEL simultaneously. The wand samples air inside a manhole, basement, or confined space BEFORE entry. Four units means multiple crew members can carry monitors. Your "is it safe to enter" instrument — most important meter on the rig for confined space and CO calls.

🧩Parts
  • Sensor block: Four electrochemical and catalytic sensors.
  • Pump: Draws sample air through the wand.
  • Sampling wand.
  • Display and alarms: Audible, visual, vibrating.
🏷️Alternate names

"4-gas," "atmospheric monitor," "Altair" (MSA), "MultiRAE," "BW" (brands).

☠️
Sample Before You Enter — Every TimeReading at the opening tells you nothing about inside. Lower the wand. Sample top, middle, bottom. Gases stratify. H₂S and LPG pool low; CH₄ rises. People die from skipping this step — routinely.
📅
Bump Test Every ShiftA monitor that hasn't been bump-tested is a monitor you can't trust. Bump test daily, calibrate per manufacturer schedule.
AED — Automated External Defibrillator
AKA: AED, defib, shock box, "the AED"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Automated external defibrillator for sudden cardiac arrest. Pads on, AED reads the rhythm, advises and delivers a shock if appropriate. Survival drops 7–10% per minute without defibrillation — every second matters. Used in every cardiac arrest until ALS arrives.

🧩Parts
  • Main unit.
  • Defibrillation pads (adult & pediatric): Verify in-date.
  • Battery: Check expiration.
  • Status indicator: Green = ready. Check every rig check.
🏷️Alternate names

"AED," "defib," "shock box," "Zoll," "LIFEPAK," "Philips."

⏱️
Rookie Mistake — Hesitating to Apply the AEDCardiac arrest confirmed → AED out, pads on. Don't wait for the medic. Every minute without defibrillation costs 7–10% survival. Now.
💧
Dry the Chest Before PadsWet chest = current path across the surface, not through the heart. Towel dry — sweat, water, blood. Bare and dry before pads go on.
2× SCBA Masks (1 Medium, 1 Small)
AKA: SCBA facepiece, air mask, face piece, "spare masks"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two spare SCBA facepieces — one medium, one small — for a crew member whose mask is damaged or doesn't fit, or for a RIT/Mayday scenario needing an additional mask for a downed firefighter. These are facepieces only — they connect to an SCBA air supply and don't carry their own tank.

🧩Parts
  • Facepiece lens: Wide-view polycarbonate.
  • Face seal: Silicone or rubber.
  • Head harness: Must be sized to the wearer before entry.
  • Regulator port.
🫁
Fit Check Before Every EntryCover the low-pressure inlet, inhale, hold. The mask collapses and holds — no leakage. Any leakage means don't enter. Facial hair breaks the seal. Beard + SCBA = not entering — this is not negotiable.
2× Fire Hoods
AKA: Nomex hood, flash hood, SCBA hood, "the hood"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Two spare Nomex hoods covering the neck, ears, and face perimeter — bridging the gap between SCBA facepiece and helmet/coat collar. Your last line of defense for facial and neck burns. A firefighter without a properly seated hood has exposed skin, and exposed skin burns.

🧩Parts
  • Nomex or PBI knit body: Inherently flame-resistant.
  • Face opening: Seats around SCBA facepiece perimeter.
  • Neck/shoulder coverage.
🔥
Rookie Mistake — Hood Not Sealed Around the MaskHood goes on BEFORE the mask. Pull mask over the hood, tuck, verify seal. A gap at the cheek or chin is unprotected skin — that skin burns in a rollover.
Caution Tape
AKA: Barrier tape, scene tape, yellow tape, "the caution tape"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Yellow plastic barrier tape for establishing a perimeter — keeping civilians out of the hazard zone and marking dangerous areas. Visual barrier only; it won't stop someone determined, but it clearly communicates "stay out" and legally demarcates the scene.

👮
Set It Early and WideSet your perimeter wider than you think you need. Bystanders push up to the tape. If your perimeter is exactly at the hazard zone, one person leaning in is inside it. Give yourself buffer.
Fire Tape
AKA: Red fire tape, fire line tape, "do not enter" tape
+
📖What it is & what it does

Red "FIRE LINE — DO NOT CROSS" tape for a fire scene perimeter or post-fire structure under investigation. Signals a higher-risk zone than yellow caution tape. Left on structures after a fire to indicate unsafe entry or active investigation.

🏚️
Right Tape for the Right SituationYellow = general scene perimeter. Red fire tape = active fire line or post-fire investigation in progress. Using the wrong one sends the wrong signal to the public and other agencies.
4× Box Lights
AKA: Portable scene lights, work lights, "the box lights"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Four portable LED box-style scene lights for illuminating work areas — interiors, extrication zones, or any nighttime scene requiring hands-free area lighting. Four units lets you spread light across a multi-task scene simultaneously.

🧩Parts
  • LED panel, housing, handle and stand/hook.
  • Power source: Battery or cord depending on model.
🔋
Verify Charge Every Rig CheckA box light with a dead battery is a paperweight. Check charge state every shift. Replace or recharge before the rig goes back in service.
Safety Vests
AKA: Hi-viz vest, reflective vest, ANSI vest, traffic vest, "the vest"
+
📖What it is & what it does

High-visibility ANSI reflective vests for roadway scene safety. Crew members NOT in full turnout gear wear a safety vest when operating at vehicle accidents on active roadways. A bright orange or lime-green ANSI vest dramatically increases conspicuity at night or in low light.

🚗
Struck-By Incidents Kill FirefightersBeing struck by a passing vehicle is a leading cause of firefighter LODDs. In the roadway, not in full turnout gear → vest goes on. Not optional.
Fire Wipes
AKA: Decon wipes, firefighter wipes, carcinogen wipes, "the wipes"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Specially formulated wipes for removing toxic fire byproducts — soot, PAHs, carcinogens — from exposed skin immediately after exiting a fire or smoke environment. Used on neck, face, and hands at the rig before removing gear, touching your face, or eating. Step one of gross decontamination.

⚕️
Cancer Is the Leading Cause of Firefighter DeathFireground carcinogen exposure accumulates over a career. Wipe at the rig after every fire — even small jobs. Then bag contaminated gear, shower before anything else at the station, and keep dirty gear out of living areas. The wipes are the first step.
Knox Box
AKA: Knox, rapid-entry key, master key, "the Knox"
+
📖What it is & what it does

The department master key that opens all Knox rapid-entry key boxes installed on commercial buildings and facilities throughout the response area. Building owners deposit a key to their property inside a tamper-resistant Knox box on their exterior wall. This master key opens ALL of them. Eliminates forced entry on commercial fire, alarm, and EMS calls at Knox-equipped buildings.

🧩Parts
  • Knox master key: Treat it like a department firearm — on the rig or secured. Never in a personal vehicle or pocket.
  • Key ring / retention.
🔑
Rookie Mistake — Mishandling the Knox KeyThis key opens every Knox box in the jurisdiction. Losing it or leaving it unsecured is a serious departmental security breach. It stays with the rig or with the officer. Period.
Passport System
AKA: Accountability board, personnel accountability system, passport board, "the passport"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A personnel accountability system where each firefighter has a laminated "passport" card handed to the IC or accountability officer upon arrival. The IC tracks who is on scene, what sector they're in, and when they enter/exit hazardous areas. If a Mayday happens, the passport system tells the IC immediately who is missing and where they were last assigned.

🧩Parts
  • Passport cards: Laminated ID card per crew member.
  • Accountability board: Where passports are organized by sector.
  • Velcro or magnetic backing.
📋
Rookie Mistake — Not Handing In Your PassportIf you don't hand your passport to accountability before entering and you go down inside, the IC doesn't know you're in there. A Mayday search starts from scratch. Hand in your passport. Every single time. It's how we find you when things go wrong.
Box Light (Front of Cab)
AKA: Officer's light, cab light, immediate access light, "the front box light"
+
📖What it is & what it does

A portable box light in the front of the cab for immediate officer or crew access on dismount. First light off the rig at a nighttime scene — in hand before the rear lights are deployed. Used for scene size-up, patient check, or directing crews in those first critical seconds.

🔦
This Light Has One Job — Be ReadyCharged, easily reachable from the officer's seat, deployable the second the door opens. If it's buried or dead, size-up happens in the dark.
TIC — Thermal Imaging Camera
AKA: TIC, thermal camera, heat camera, "the TIC," "the thermal"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Detects infrared radiation (heat) and displays a real-time image showing temperature differences — see through smoke, locate victims, find hidden fire, detect hot spots during overhaul, navigate in zero visibility. One of the most critical life-safety tools on the rig. The TIC detects heat radiating through walls — it does not "see through" them.

🧩Parts
  • IR sensor array.
  • Display screen.
  • Ruggedized heat-resistant housing.
  • Battery pack.
🏷️Alternate names

"TIC," "thermal," "thermal imager," "IR camera," "FLIR" (brand-as-generic), "Scott Eagle" (brand).

🔥
Rookie Mistake — Trusting the TIC Without Understanding Its LimitsThe TIC shows relative heat — not absolute temperature. A victim-shaped heat signature doesn't confirm a living victim. The TIC guides your search; it doesn't replace hands-on assessment. And it can't see through water, mirrors, or certain materials.
🏠
TIC Goes In — Every Interior FireA crew going interior without a TIC is operating blind. If the battery is dead and there's no spare charged pack, that's a pre-shift failure. Report it and fix it before you go.
Fuel Keys
AKA: Fleet card, fuel card, gas keys, "the fuel keys"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Keys or fleet card for accessing municipality or department fuel pumps. Stored in the front of the cab for driver access. Squad 61 burns significant fuel on runs and pump operations — the fuel keys ensure the driver can refuel at authorized stations without hunting for authorization.

⛽
Refuel at Three-Quarters — Not EmptyA rig that returns at a quarter-tank and doesn't get refueled before the next run may not make the scene. Department policy: refuel any time you drop below three-quarters. Don't leave a fuel problem for the next crew.
Safety Flares
AKA: Road flares, fusees, emergency flares, "the flares"
+
📖What it is & what it does

Pyrotechnic road flares for traffic control at roadway incidents. Placed upstream in a taper pattern to warn approaching drivers to slow and move over. Visible in rain and fog, stays lit in high wind. At a nighttime MVA on an unlit road, properly placed flares are the difference between a controlled scene and a secondary crash.

🧩Parts
  • Flare body.
  • Cap / striker: Strike-anywhere ignition.
  • Spike (some models).
  • Burn time label: 15, 20, or 30 minutes typical.
🏷️Alternate names

"Fusees," "road flares," "highway flares." LED alternatives: "LED flares," "electronic flares."

⛽
Rookie Mistake — Pyrotechnic Flares Near Fuel SpillsA pyrotechnic flare at a fuel-spill scene is an ignition source. If fuel is on the roadway, use LED/electronic flares — not pyrotechnic. Know what's on the ground before you strike a flare.
📏
Start Your Taper Far BackOn a highway at 55 mph, a driver needs 1,500+ feet of warning to react. Place your first flare far upstream and taper toward the scene. Not 50 feet back.
